items.name: Amber ledger and the lint rule
items.purpose: NEW, added because the critic proved the old accounting was unlintable: one place that defines what counts as an amber object and how many a composed frame may hold.
items.anatomy: An amber OBJECT is any painted region whose colour is flame-500/600/700/900 and whose area exceeds 64dp², or any stroke of those colours longer than 24dp. A rim plus its top-edge gradient bleed on the same widget is ONE object. Six target ticks of the same class across six bars are counted individually — which is why only one of them may be amber. The lint counts objects in the COMPOSED FRAME, not per route: a floating nav pill is in frame on every tab root and is counted there. Budget: 2 in Night, 1 in Day and Veld, 0 on any screen with no expected next move.
items.states: NIGHT: amber may be a rim, a gradient stop, a stroke, an underline, a focus rule, a single target tick, or a filled block whose foreground is #0B1017 (10.65:1). DAY/VELD: amber may be one filled block with dark ink, and it must be the widget registered as that route's primary commit action — nothing else, ever. ARMED: an action circle takes amber only when it is the expected next move. TAB ROOT, NIGHT: the active nav pill is object #1 by owner decision, so the screen has at most one other. TAB ROOT, DAY/VELD: the pill is an ink block, never amber; a screen with nothing armed has ZERO amber.
items.behaviour: A lint failure fails the build, not the review. Each widget that may paint amber registers an AmberIntent with a reason string; the test harness renders every route in three skins at 1.0× and 2.0×, walks the layer tree, and asserts the count and the reason.
items.modes: The budget is the mode difference: Night 2, Day 1, Veld 1. Veld additionally forbids amber as stroke, border, glyph or text at any size (#FFB162 on white is 1.79:1).
items.accessibility: Amber is never announced, never named, and never the only carrier of anything — every amber object has a word beside it. A screen reader user never learns that amber exists, and loses nothing.
items.amber: This item defines the budget; it paints none.
items.screenshot: Not a screen — a rule. Its visible evidence is that on any frame you can point at the one or two warm things and say what they are for.

items.name: Meaning-bearing glyph scale rule
items.purpose: NEW, from the critique: the whole anti-colour-only defence rests on shape, and every shape was pinned in dp, so the low-vision agent got shape at a quarter of its intended optical weight.
items.anatomy: Two classes. MEANING-BEARING (scales with textScaler, clamped at 2.0×): the delta triangle 8→16, the state dot/square/triangle 12→24, the finding triangle 8→16, the flag glyph 16→32, the section state tile 28→48 with its glyph 16→32, the radio ring 28→48, the check box 28→48, the skin-cycle glyph 24→48 with its target growing 56→72. DECORATIVE (fixed): the ladder hairlines, the empty-state line drawing, the grabber, the chevron (18dp; it is redundant with the row's own tappability). PARTIAL (half rate): progress and meter tracks, 8→12dp, because a 16dp track is a slab, not a rule — the meaning in a bar lives in its tick and its words, both of which scale fully.
items.states: 1.0× baseline. 1.3×–2.0× linear. Above 2.0× clamped, matching every other clamp in the system. Veld applies its own floors first, then the scaler on top.
items.behaviour: One helper, glyphScale(context), used by every painter. No component re-litigates it. CustomPaint sizes come from the helper, not from constants, so a glyph cannot be checked in pinned.
items.modes: Veld starts one step up (28dp tiles become 32dp) and scales from there, so Veld at 2.0× is the largest case in the system and is the one measured on device.
items.accessibility: This rule IS the accessibility fix: the user who most needs shape-not-hue is the user running 2.0×, and they were getting the weakest shapes. Glyph growth never changes semantics or announcement order.
items.amber: None.
items.screenshot: The same stat tile twice: at 1.0× a small solid triangle beside '47'; at 2.0× a triangle twice the height beside a doubled figure, still in proportion.

items.name: Agent shell (AgentScaffold)
items.purpose: The chrome every agent screen wears: a header that is capped, a scrolling body, and a bottom region whose shape depends on whether the screen is a tab root.
items.anatomy: Gutter 20 (s5, Veld 24) set once as side padding on one outer wrapper; vertical padding always padding-block. HEADER min 96dp: optional 48dp back chevron (2px stroke, ink-2); title at title.l 24/600/1.25 Onest ink-1, wraps to 2 lines, middle-truncates at 3; 8dp; subtitle at label 13/400/1.35 ink-2 — REVISED, now capped at 2 lines then tail-truncated, because an Afrikaans subtitle at 2.0× was taking 130dp of a 640dp viewport. Sync chip pinned right of the title row, top-aligned, intrinsic width. Flag-chip Wrap 12dp beneath — REVISED, capped at 2 rows, then a 44dp 'and 2 more' expander row that expands in place. HEADER CEILING, NEW: 40% of viewport height. Past it the header stops being pinned and scrolls with the body as a sliver, so the body always keeps 60%. BODY: ListView, padding top 16, bottom 24 plus the bottom region's height. BOTTOM REGION, REVISED — three shapes, one of which always applies. (1) TAB ROOT: no thumb zone; a single floating 64dp row, inset 16 both gutters, 20dp above the safe area, holding [skin cycle 56] [8] [nav pill, Expanded] [8] [action circle 64]. (2) SCREEN WITH A PRIMARY ACTION: a fixed 96dp thumb zone, 1px hairline across the full bleed, then [skin cycle 56] [12] [primary, Expanded, 56dp]. (3) SCREEN WITH NO PRIMARY ACTION: a 76dp zone holding the skin cycle alone at the leading gutter — never a hairline over nothing, and never a screen without the skin cycle.
items.states: Default. Scrolled (the header does not collapse, blur or swap fill unless it has hit the 40% ceiling, in which case it scrolls away entirely). No back (chevron slot collapses to zero). Two thumb actions (primary 56dp, a second ghost 56dp above at 8dp, zone 160dp). Keyboard open (the zone lifts with the inset and never scrolls away). Signed-out (a persistent 44dp line under the header: square glyph, 'Signed out — work is saving locally', inline 44dp ghost 'Sign in'). 2.0× (header grows to its ceiling then scrolls; thumb zone 128dp; the skin cycle grows to 72dp under the glyph-scale rule).
items.behaviour: Push into a section slides from the right, 320ms, enter curve (0.05,0.70,0.10,1.00). REVISED: the body-children stagger is CUT from every push — the critic is right that arrival order encoded nothing and bought the worst frame window of the visit nine times a store. The stagger survives in exactly one place, first app open on Today, where it is the app waking up rather than a transition. No pull-to-refresh inside a visit; Today and My work have it. Slow data renders the skeleton; wrong data keeps the chrome and puts the failure in the body.
items.modes: Night: ground #0B1017, hairline #3A4B60. Day: ground #EEE9DF, hairline #DED7C9, one sh1 under the thumb zone only. Veld: ground #FFFFFF, ink #0E141A, gutter 24, the thumb-zone rule a 2px solid #1B2632, primary 64dp, zone 112dp, type steps up per the Veld scale with a 600 weight floor.
items.accessibility: Header title is Semantics(header:true). Back chevron carries 'Back to {destination}', never 'Back'. Targets ≥48 Field / ≥56 Veld. Nothing is pinned at 2.0× — every region is min-height. Reading order: header, flag chips, body, bottom region last. The bottom region is a Semantics container labelled 'Actions'.
items.amber: None. The shell hosts its screen's amber; it never paints any.
items.screenshot: A phone screen with a store name top-left in warm off-white, a grey line under it, a small outlined '12 held' chip at the right, a long quiet list, and — floating clear of the bottom edge, not welded to it — a small square moon button, a dark four-slot bar, and a circle.

items.name: Thumb zone with skin cycle
items.purpose: Puts the skin toggle and the one primary action in the only region a one-handed agent holding a crate can reach — and guarantees the skin cycle is on every screen including tab roots.
items.anatomy: SKIN CYCLE: 56×56 (Veld 64, 2.0× 72), radius 10. Night well #141D27 with a 1px edge-control #7C93AC; Day well #E2DBCC with 1px #6E6657; Veld white with 2px #1B2632. Glyph 24px, 2px stroke, ink-1, scaling to 48 at 2.0×: sun = Veld, paper = Day, moon = Night. No label at rest; the label is the semanticLabel and the long-press sheet. In a thumb zone it sits at the leading gutter with the primary Expanded beside it at 12dp. On a tab root it sits at the leading end of the floating row — REVISED, this is the fix for the collision the critic found: previously Today and My work specified both a 96dp zone and a 64dp floating pill, which was either 200dp of permanent chrome or no skin cycle at all on the screen the agent lives on.
items.states: Three cycle positions, each a different glyph, never a colour alone. Pressed: scale 0.98 over 120ms plus the fill stepping to lifted / raised / a solid #1B2632 with a white glyph in Veld. Pre-armed (the agent chose Veld at this outlet at this hour last visit): the sun glyph with a 2px edge-control ring offset 3dp, plus a one-time 44dp line 'Veld is on — you used it here last time.' with a 44dp ghost 'Use Day instead'. Disabled: never.
items.behaviour: Tap cycles Day → Veld → Night → Day, 120ms, no full-screen cross-fade (that reads as a crash on a 2GB handset) — the ThemeExtension swap is instant, only the glyph animates. Buzz.tick. Long-press opens a 3-row sheet naming the three skins. Veld exits on this control, on a check-in at a new outlet, or on sustained low ambient — never on idle.
items.modes: Deliberately near-identical in all three: it is the door between them. Veld makes it 64×64 with a 2px border and kills the press scale.
items.accessibility: Semantics(toggled:) with 'Screen: Day. Double-tap for Veld, the outdoor high-contrast screen.' — the NEXT state is named. 56dp exceeds the 48 Field floor and meets Veld's 56 floor; 72dp at 2.0×. Announces the new skin as a live region.
items.amber: None, ever.
items.screenshot: A small square button with a thin outlined moon, sitting left of a wide amber block with dark text reading 'Check in here'.

items.name: Floating nav pill and action circle
items.purpose: Agent home navigation — four tabs floating above the content, the primary move as a separate circle, and the skin cycle on the same row so there is one bottom object rather than two.
items.anatomy: One floating row, 64dp, inset 16 from both gutters, 20dp above the safe area: [skin cycle 56] [8] [PILL, Expanded, 64dp, radius 14, fill well #141D27 fully opaque, zero BackdropFilter] [8] [CIRCLE 64dp]. Pill holds four equal slots: 24px 2px-stroke icon over an 11/700/+8% label. Active slot: a 48dp radius-10 solid pill inset 8dp, label weight 700, plus a 2dp silhouette overshoot past the bar's bottom edge so the state has an outline in greyscale. Inactive: nav-ink-inactive #8AA0B8 at 500 (6.32:1 on the nav body). Circle: 2px-stroke glyph 24px, a store-with-a-plus. Tabs: Today, My work, Map, Me. WIDTH: at 360dp the pill gets 192dp, four 48dp icon-only slots; labels appear from 400dp at 61dp slots.
items.states: Active / inactive. Circle ARMED (amber fill, ground ink) only when an unplanned visit is the expected next move — route finished, or stationary inside an unplanned outlet's fence. UNARMED (transparent, 2px edge-control ring, ink-1 glyph) otherwise, which is most of the day. Badge: My work carries a mono 11/700 count in an 18dp radius-6 tile when something needs the agent, never for the ordinary held count. Pressed: scale 0.98. Offline: unchanged. Inside a visit: the whole component is ABSENT. LARGE TEXT, REVISED: at 1.3× the pill grows to 76dp with labels at their scaled size; at ≥1.6× it becomes a 2×2 grid, 132dp tall, full width on its own row, with the skin cycle and circle on a row beneath. Icon-only is the fallback for NARROW SCREENS only. KEPT AGAINST ONE NUMBER IN THE CRITIQUE: the critic called the active pill's remaining signal 'a 1.50:1 adjacent-fill relationship'. It is not — #FFB162 on well #141D27 is 9.49:1 in Night and #2C3B4D on #E2DBCC is 8.28:1 in Day. The fill channel was always strong; the failure was stripping the words from the user who asked for bigger words, and that is what I have fixed.
items.behaviour: Tap switches tab with no page transition; the body cross-fades 200ms and the active slot slides 200ms. Circle tap opens the outlet picker as a sheet, not a route. Long-press the circle: nothing.
items.modes: Night — active pill flame-600 #FFB162 with #0B1017 ink (10.65:1); it is object #1 of the frame's two. Day — active pill solid lifted #2C3B4D with #EEE9DF ink (9.43:1). Veld — bar white with a 2px #1B2632 border, active slot a solid #1B2632 block with white ink (15.33:1), 72dp tall, labels 13/700; armed circle amber #FFB162 with #0E141A (10.34:1).
items.accessibility: Each slot is Semantics(selected:, button:) reading 'Today, tab 1 of 4, selected'. The circle takes a required non-empty semanticLabel — a required constructor argument, so the 26 unlabelled IconButtons cannot recur.
items.amber: REVISED, and this withdraws the clause I invented. DAY AND VELD: the pill is NEVER amber. A light-ground screen with nothing armed has ZERO amber — the same rule that already governs My visits and every empty state. The amber block on a light ground is only ever the primary commit action, which is what the direction spec says and what I had quietly amended. NIGHT: the pill is amber by owner decision and is counted as object #1 on every tab root, so a Night tab root has at most one other amber object.
items.screenshot: Floating clear of the bottom edge: a small square moon button, a wide dark rounded bar with four icons and labels whose leftmost sits in a solid amber lozenge with near-black text, and a dark circle with a thin store-plus glyph.

items.name: Sync chip
items.purpose: Answers the question an agent asks all day — is my work safe? — without ever calling the normal state an error.
items.anatomy: Height 44 (Field 48, Veld 56), radius 6, 1px edge-control, transparent fill over the well, padding 12/8. Leading 12dp glyph (24dp at 2.0× under the glyph-scale rule), 8dp, the count in JetBrains Mono 13/500 and the word in Onest label 13/500 ink-2 — 'held on this phone'. Tappable, opens My work.
items.states: ALL SENT — mint outline, filled circle, 'All sent'. HELD (normal) — filled SQUARE in ink-2, '12 held on this phone'; never red, never a severity. SENDING — three 6px Oatmeal dots on a 600ms loop, 'Sending 12'. STUCK — 1px bad outline, half-filled triangle, '2 need you'. NEVER-SIGNED-IN — does not render. LOADING — a well-filled block at the chip's exact geometry.
items.behaviour: Updates from a stream, so it never needs a pull-to-refresh. Tap → My work, 320ms. Suppressed on the screen it opens. The dots are one of three subscribers on the single application Ticker, stop the instant the flush ends, and are killed by reduce-motion, battery-saver and Veld.
items.modes: Night: ink-2 #C9C1B1 on well #141D27, edge #7C93AC. Day: ink-2 #4A4437, edge #6E6657, well #E2DBCC. Veld: 56dp, white fill, 2px #1B2632, label 16/600; stuck takes a solid #7A0F22 block with white ink (10.94:1); no dot animation, the word 'Sending' alone.
items.accessibility: Semantics(button:true, label:'12 captures held on this phone. Double-tap to see your work.') — the state word leads. Stuck announces 'Needs you' first. Shape (circle/square/triangle) carries the state in greyscale and scales to 24dp at 2.0×.
items.amber: None. A status chip is exactly what the amber law forbids amber from being.
items.screenshot: Top-right of the header: a small outlined lozenge with a tiny solid square and '12 held on this phone' in muted oatmeal.

items.name: Soft row
items.purpose: The one full-width surface every agent list is built from — a subtle fill, not a bordered box, so a list of eleven does not read as eleven boxes.
items.anatomy: Full bleed to the gutter, min-height 64, padding 16 horizontal inside the gutter, 12 vertical. Leading slot 28 or 40dp, 12dp, a text column (title.m 16/600 ink-1 wrapping to 2, then meta 12/400/1.40 ink-3), 8dp, a trailing column (figure.s 16/600 mono over an 11/700 state word, or an 18dp chevron). Radius 0 in a list; a row that stands alone takes radius 14 and a surface fill. SEPARATION, REVISED — this is the blocker fix. A 1px rule inset 56dp to the leading text edge, and its colour now depends on whether the row is a CONTROL: between TAPPABLE rows it is edge-structure (#5A7088 Night, 3.73:1 on ground; #857C6B Day, 3.41:1 on Palladian), because a tappable row is a UI component and 1.4.11 wants a perceivable boundary; between non-tappable rows it stays hairline-decorative. The old universal 1.18:1 Day hairline turned an 11-stop route in sun into one paragraph of store names. KEPT AGAINST THE CRITIQUE'S FRAMING: the critic said to 'drop the no-borders purity for lists'. I have not. A 1px inset rule is not a border and does not box a row; the fix was a contrast fix, not a structural retreat, and the left gutter stays open so the list still reads as a column of text rather than a grid.
items.states: Default (transparent over ground). Pressed (fill steps to raised, 120ms, plus scale 0.99 on the leading tile). Non-tappable (no chevron, no press fill, decorative separator — the absence is the signal). Selected (1px edge-control inside plus a 2px-stroke tick). Severity-bearing (a 3px left bar at full row height in bad; watch level 40% height; fine = absent). Disabled (ink-mute text, no press, and the reason in the meta line). Loading (well-filled blocks at the exact text geometry). Last in group (no rule).
items.behaviour: const-constructible, ColoredBox plus a 1px Divider, no shadow, gradient or blur. Press feedback is fill plus a haptic tick, never a Material ripple travelling 300dp. Long-press only where a row has a second verb, and then it opens a sheet.
items.modes: Night: transparent over ground, tappable rule #5A7088, pressed fill #22303E. Day: transparent over #EEE9DF, tappable rule #857C6B, pressed fill #F4F0E8. Veld: rules become 2px solid #1B2632 full bleed, min-height 64 with a 600 weight floor, and the press is a solid #1B2632 fill with white text for its duration — no tint step survives sunlight.
items.accessibility: One Semantics node per row, not four: 'Kasi Corner Spaza, 1.2 kilometres, next stop. Double-tap to check in.' Severity announces first. The row is the target, always ≥64dp. At 2.0× the text column grows and the trailing column drops beneath it rather than squeezing the name.
items.amber: None. Rows never carry amber — that is what stops the repeated-fill violation that kills this law in practice.
items.screenshot: A quiet full-width band of text on the page ground: a small outlined square, a store name, a grey line under it, '1.2 km' right-aligned in a monospaced face, and a fine grey rule beneath starting where the text starts.

items.name: Section state glyph — four states
items.purpose: Says where a section stands, in a shape a colour-blind agent reads at arm's length in a dark aisle.
items.anatomy: 28dp square tile (Veld 32, 2.0× 48), radius 6, 2px border, glyphs 2px-stroke 16px (32 at 2.0×), centred. REVISED: the 2px vertical rule that joined the tiles into a ladder is DELETED — see behaviour.
items.states: REVISED — four states, four silhouettes, because the critic correctly found two empty boxes. 1 NOT STARTED — 2px edge-control border, transparent fill, NO glyph; detail line reads 'Not started' or 'Optional'. 2 IN PROGRESS — the same border plus a HALF-DISC GLYPH: a 16dp circle whose leading half is a solid ink-1 fill and whose trailing half is a 2px ring. This is the glyph the app already draws today (tick / half-circle / empty ring) and I should not have dropped it for a fill step: lifted #2C3B4D over ground #0B1017 is 1.67:1, and over the well 1.49:1, well under the device floor, so a half-filled tile and an empty tile were the same object at 40% backlight. The half-fill of the TILE stays as reinforcement, never as the state. The row still carries the count, '3 of 12'. 3 DONE — solid good fill (#6FE0AE Night, #14664A Day), 2px-stroke tick in the ground ink. 4 CAN'T CONFIRM — hatch, not colour: 45° hard-stop stripes, 2px/3px, chart-neutral #8B8271 over the well, 2px edge-control border, an em-dash glyph. Not red, not amber, not a failure; the row names the reason in words. SCORE ROW (a fifth, non-section case) — hatched tile with an em dash, no border highlight, not tappable.
items.behaviour: Done animates: the tick draws over 200ms the first time a section completes — the small win an agent gets seven times a visit. The other three are static; hatch never animates. Reduce-motion and Veld set the tick instantly. THE LADDER RULE IS GONE: the hub says twice that sections can be done in any order, and a 2px rule wiring seven tiles top-to-bottom said the opposite louder than a 12px hint said it. A column of tiles already reads as a set.
items.modes: Night: border #7C93AC, half-disc ink-1 #EEE9DF, done #6FE0AE with a #0B1017 tick, hatch #8B8271. Day: border #6E6657, half-disc #1B2632, done #14664A with a #FAF7F2 tick, hatch #676052. Veld: 32dp tile, 2px #1B2632 border, half-disc solid #1B2632, done a solid #0F5039 with a white tick, hatch in #1B2632 stripes on white — hatch is the state that survives Veld best, which is why it was chosen for the ambiguous case.
items.accessibility: semanticLabel per state, in the same token as the glyph: 'Not started' / 'In progress, 3 of 12' / 'Done' / "Can't confirm — store refused". The tile is never the tap target; the whole 64dp row is. Tile and glyph scale to 48/32 at 2.0×.
items.amber: None. Section state is a status, and status is where amber is banned.
items.screenshot: A column of small rounded squares, no longer wired together: two solid green with white ticks, one carrying a half-filled disc, two empty outlines, one filled with fine diagonal stripes and a dash.

items.name: Flag chip
items.purpose: States a fact about a visit — out of fence, flagged for review, unfinished — without making it a verdict.
items.anatomy: Height 44 (Field 48, Veld 56), radius 6, 1px edge-control, transparent fill, padding 12/0. A 16px 2px-stroke glyph (32 at 2.0×), 8dp, label 13/500 ink-2, and any measured figure in JetBrains Mono 13/500 ('Out of fence · 180 m'). Laid out in a Wrap under the header, 8dp gaps, REVISED — capped at 2 rows, then a 44dp 'and 2 more' expander that expands in place, because an uncapped Wrap plus a 2-line title plus a subtitle was a 370dp non-scrolling header at 2.0× in Afrikaans.
items.states: OUT OF FENCE — broken-ring glyph, neutral, distance in mono. FLAGGED FOR REVIEW — square-with-a-dot, neutral, tappable to who and when. UNFINISHED VISIT — half-ring, neutral, tappable to the decision sheet. NOT CONFIRMED ×N (NEW) — hatched glyph, neutral, '3 sections not confirmed', tappable to the list; it exists so a manager sees the shape of a visit that was answered rather than captured. SENT BACK — the one genuine severity, because a human rejected the work: 1px bad outline, bad ink, half-filled triangle, tappable to the manager's note. PRESSED — fill steps to raised. NON-TAPPABLE — no press fill. STALE — a flag older than 7 days appends its date.
items.behaviour: Tap opens a sheet, not a dialog. Flags never dismiss themselves and the agent cannot clear one. Beyond two rows they collapse to a counted expander rather than truncating, so nothing is hidden, only folded.
items.modes: Night: edge #7C93AC, ink-2 #C9C1B1; Sent back in bad #FF7D8C. Day: edge #6E6657, ink-2 #4A4437; Sent back #8C1B2C. Veld: 56dp, 2px #1B2632, label 16/600; Sent back becomes a SOLID #7A0F22 block with white ink (10.94:1) — a 2px crimson outline on white is the first thing sunlight eats.
items.accessibility: Label leads with the fact: 'Out of fence, 180 metres. Double-tap for detail.' Sent back leads with the severity word. Glyph shape differs per kind so the row reads in greyscale and under deuteranopia, and scales to 32dp at 2.0×. The expander announces 'Show 2 more flags'.
items.amber: Never. A flag is a label, and amber is not a label.
items.screenshot: Under a store name, two small outlined lozenges: one with a broken-circle glyph reading 'Out of fence · 180 m', one with a square-and-dot reading 'Flagged for review'.

items.name: Primary and secondary action button
items.purpose: The one thing to do next, and everything else.
items.anatomy: PRIMARY — height 56 (Veld 64), radius 10, full width of the gutter minus the skin cycle, label REVISED to 16/600 (Veld 18/700): the commit action was carrying the smallest type on the screen, below body at 15 and below Veld's own 16 label floor, and the button is 56–64dp tall so the fix is free. Optional 18px 2px-stroke trailing glyph at 8dp. SECONDARY (ghost) — same heights, transparent, 1px edge-control (Veld 2px #1B2632), ink-1 label, never any amber. DESTRUCTIVE ghost — 1px bad outline, bad ink, and the label always names the consequence ('Delete and start over').
items.states: DEFAULT. PRESSED — REVISED, and this was the blocker: Night's press stepped the fill to flame-500 while Night's ink is Palladian #EEE9DF, which is 1.83:1 — worse than the 2.00:1 failure the old spec congratulated itself on fixing, and invisible at 40% backlight for the 120ms of the commit. Night now presses by FLOODING: the 1px amber rim fills the button, giving a solid flame-600 #FFB162 with #0B1017 ink at 10.65:1. It is the largest possible change on a cheap panel, it is legal under the Night lint rule, and it means what it should — the light source floods the plate at the moment of commitment. Day presses to flame-500 keeping #1B2632 ink (6.91:1). Veld inverts to a solid #1B2632 block with white ink (15.33:1), no scale. All three keep scale 0.98 over 120ms except Veld, which has no motion. BUSY — the label is replaced by three 6px Oatmeal dots on a 600ms loop; never a spinner, and the button keeps its size. DISABLED — well fill, ink-mute #4C6079, no rim, no amber, and a BarNote directly above naming exactly what is missing. SUCCESS — no green flash; busy, then the route changes. FAILED — the button returns to default and a bad-outlined line names the reason and what survived.
items.behaviour: Buzz.tick on press, Buzz.done on a commit that ends a visit. Double-tap protection: busy on the first tap, the second ignored. An irreversible commit never fires from a single tap on a hub — it routes through a gate screen.
items.modes: Night: rest is lifted #2C3B4D, 1px flame-600 rim, Palladian ink (9.43:1), plus a 2px amber gradient bleed along the top edge (#FFF1DE@0.55 → #FFB162@0.30 → transparent) — amber as emitted light, one object. Day: solid #FFB162 with #1B2632 ink (8.55:1). Veld: solid #FFB162 with #0E141A (10.34:1), 64dp, 18/700, no gradient, no rim, no scale.
items.accessibility: Semantics(button:, enabled:). A disabled button keeps its label and appends the blocking reason, so a screen-reader user is never told only 'dimmed'. Busy is a liveRegion announcing 'Sending'. At 2.0× the label wraps to two lines and the button grows to 88dp rather than truncating.
items.amber: One, and it is the point: the primary action is where the agent's amber budget goes. A screen never has two primaries.
items.screenshot: A wide warm-amber block with near-black centred text reading 'Submit this visit' at a size that matches the section names above it, and below a transparent outlined block reading 'Go back and change something'.

items.name: Count stepper
items.purpose: Enter a shelf count one-handed, without looking at the phone, where zero is a finding and not an empty box.
items.anatomy: REVISED LAYOUT — the critic is right that [−] and [+] at opposite margins is 250dp of grip-shift per adjustment, twelve times a bay, for an agent with a crate on their other arm. Now: the value trough Expanded at the LEADING edge, then an adjacent pair [−][+] at the trailing edge, 56×56 each (Veld 64), separated by a 1px edge-control rule — the arrangement of every till and fuel pump in the country. A handedness preference in Me ('Which hand do you hold the phone in?') mirrors the whole control once. Trough: well fill, radius 10 at the BOTTOM corners and 0 at the top, 1px bottom rule in edge-control, the value in JetBrains Mono figure.m 22/600 (Veld 24/600), tabular, aligned to the trough's leading padding so it sits under the SKU name. Step glyphs 2px-stroke 20px, ink-1.
items.states: NOT COUNTED (null) — an em dash in ink-3 plus a 12/400 ink-3 line reading 'not counted', so a bare dash is never the whole message. COUNTED. ZERO / FINDING — a 3px bad left bar at the SKU block's full height, the figure in bad with a filled triangle to its left (scaling to 16px at 2.0×), and a note: 'Out of stock. This raises a task for the manager.' PRESSED — fill raised, 120ms, scale 0.98. AT MIN — [−] disabled, and from 'not counted' the first [−] means 'there are none', an explicit zero. AT MAX — [+] disabled. TYPING — tapping the value opens a number sheet: the SKU name as title.m, one trough, 'Cancel' ghost, 'Set' amber. SAVE FAILED — the value is untouched; the failure is a line, not a reset.
items.behaviour: Buzz.tick on every step; Buzz.finding — heavier and longer — the moment a value lands on zero, because the agent is looking at the shelf and zero is the most valuable thing they can record. Long-press a step: 400ms hold, then 8/second with a tick every fifth. Tap the number to type it; ± is for adjusting.
items.modes: Night: trough well #141D27, rule #7C93AC, figure #EEE9DF, finding #FF7D8C. Day: trough #E2DBCC, rule #6E6657, finding #8C1B2C. Veld: 64dp, white fill, 2px #1B2632 on all parts, figure 24/600, press a solid #1B2632 with a white glyph, and the finding is a 4px #7A0F22 left bar plus the word with no tint at all.
items.accessibility: The whole stepper is one Semantics node with value 'Units on shelf, 12. Swipe up to increase, down to decrease' plus increased/decreasedActions, so a screen-reader user never hunts a 56dp target. Zero announces 'Zero — out of stock, this raises a task'. Steps carry 'One fewer' / 'One more'. At 2.0× the trough takes the full width on top and the ± pair sits beneath it as two 56dp halves — still adjacent.
items.amber: None — not even on [+]. A repeated amber down a 12-SKU list is the exact repeated-fill violation the law bans.
items.screenshot: A wide control: a flat-topped trough on the left holding '12' in a monospaced face, and at the right a joined pair of square minus and plus buttons. Beneath, a second one holding '0' in crimson with a small solid triangle, and a red bar down the left edge of the whole product block.

items.name: Trough input and field grammar
items.purpose: Every typed value in the app — a number, a price, a note — in one shape that reads as a container that holds things.
items.anatomy: Label ABOVE at 13/500 ink-2, never a floating placeholder. 8dp. The trough: well fill, radius 10 at the BOTTOM corners and 0 at the top, 1px bottom rule edge-control, min-height 56 (Veld 64), padding 12. Value in JetBrains Mono figure.m 22/600 for figures, Onest body 15/400 for prose. Unit or currency suffix inside the trough, right, 13/500 ink-3. Notes: min 3 lines, growing to 8, then scrolling internally.
items.states: EMPTY — visibly empty, no ghost text. FOCUSED — the bottom rule becomes 2px flame-700 #FFCB94 with a 6px gradient bloom below (Night only); in Day and Veld the focus is a 3px offset outer ring in ink-1, never amber. FILLED. ERROR — bottom rule 2px bad, a filled triangle and the message at 12/500 beneath, and the entered value is KEPT. DISABLED — well fill at ink-mute, with the reason beside the label. COUNTER — appears only past 80% of the limit. LOCALE — one NumberFormat: an Afrikaans agent sees '1 284 990,5'; null renders as an em dash with the label intact; zero renders as '0' and is never suppressed; negatives take a true minus.
items.behaviour: Tapping the trough or its label focuses it. Keyboard type is chosen per field and the decimal separator follows the locale. The bottom region lifts with the keyboard; the focused field scrolls to 96dp above it. Saving is explicit and inline.
items.modes: Night: well #141D27, rule #7C93AC, focus flame-700 plus bloom. Day: well #E2DBCC, rule #6E6657, focus a 3px #1B2632 offset ring. Veld: white fill, 2px #1B2632 on all sides, 64dp, value 24/600, focus a 3px #1B2632 offset ring — no glow, no gradient, nothing under 9:1.
items.accessibility: The label is bound to the field, announced on focus and again on error. Error text is a liveRegion. The focus indicator is 2px minimum and never colour-only — the rule thickens 1px→2px and Veld adds a physical offset ring. At 2.0× the label wraps and the trough grows.
items.amber: At most one per screen, Night only: the focused field's bottom rule. Only one field can be focused, so it cannot multiply. Day and Veld: none.
items.screenshot: A small oatmeal label 'Units on shelf' over a recessed panel with square top corners and rounded bottom ones, holding '24' in a monospaced face, with a warm amber line glowing softly along its bottom edge.

items.name: Stat tile that admits no data
items.purpose: Show a figure, or admit honestly that there isn't one — never a fake zero, and never a delta arrow next to nothing.
items.anatomy: No card, no border, no shadow. A cell in a cluster divided by 1px hairlines, not gaps. Padding 16. Eyebrow at 11/700/1.10/+8% uppercase ink-2. 8dp. Figure in JetBrains Mono figure.l 32/600 ink-1, tabular, count-up 600ms ease-out-quart. On the baseline beside it, the delta: an 8px SOLID TRIANGLE (up/down/flat) scaling to 16px at 2.0×, plus the value at 13/600 in good or bad. Optional 3px meter beneath (8→12dp at 2.0×): track lifted, fill chart-neutral, and a 2px flame-600 target tick breaking the track's top edge by 2px.
items.states: HAS DATA. NO DATA — the figure is an EM DASH in ink-3 at the same 32/600 so the cluster does not jump, the eyebrow stays, and the delta area carries the WORDS 'no visits in this window'. No triangle, no arrow, no zero, no '0%'. GENUINE ZERO — renders '0' with a FLAT triangle and the words 'no change', so missing and zero are visibly different things. LOADING — a well-filled block at the figure's exact geometry; after 600ms one Oatmeal 2px rule travels the top at 1400ms linear. STALE — a square glyph and 'as of 07:00'. PARTIAL — 'as of 3 of 5 days'. LONG FIGURE — ≤3 glyphs stay at 32, 4–6 drop to 22, 7+ to 16 with the unit demoted to a 13/500 suffix; compact formatting fires before the fitting rule, so 'R 1,28 mln' is four glyphs and stays big.
items.behaviour: Count-up runs once per visible cluster from one AnimationController, not one per tile, and is an instant set under reduce-motion, battery-saver and Veld. The target tick does not animate. Tapping a tile, where it exists, opens the underlying list, never a tooltip.
items.modes: Night: eyebrow #C9C1B1, figure #EEE9DF, hairline #3A4B60, track #2C3B4D, fill #8B8271, tick #FFB162. Day: #4A4437, #1B2632, #DED7C9, #E2DBCC, #676052, tick 2px #1B2632. Veld: figure 34/600, eyebrow 13/700, the hairline a 2px #1B2632 rule, the meter a 6dp track with a 2px border and a solid fill, the tick a 3px mark.
items.accessibility: One sentence per cell: 'Visits this week, 47, up 6.' No data reads 'Visits this week, no data, no visits in this window' — never a bare dash. Direction is the word 'up'/'down'/'no change', never a glyph name. At 2.0× the figure and delta stack via a Wrap and the cluster collapses to one column.
items.amber: At most one in Night — the target tick on one meter, and only where a target genuinely exists. Zero in Day and Veld.
items.screenshot: Two cells split by a hairline: left, 'VISITS THIS WEEK' over '47' in big monospaced digits with a solid up-triangle and '6'; right, 'AVERAGE SCORE' over a long em dash in grey with 'no visits in this window' beneath.

items.name: Person row
items.purpose: Name a human — and never print a raw database id as the thing an agent reads first.
items.anatomy: Soft row, 64dp min. Leading 40dp radius-6 tile holding initials at 16/700 ink-1 on the well — not a photo (POPIA, plus 40dp of bundle per person); a 2px-stroke person glyph when initials are unknown. 12dp. Primary line: name at title.m 16/600, wrapping to 2, middle-truncating at 3. Secondary: meta 12/400 ink-3, role then outlet. Separators are inserted only between parts that exist, so there is never a dangling '·'. Trailing: a state word at 11/700 or an 18dp chevron.
items.states: FULL. NO NAME — the primary line becomes the role and outlet, and the id renders as a SECONDARY line in mono.ident 13/500 ink-3 prefixed 'id'. A UUID is never the primary line. NO ROLE / NO OUTLET — the meta line collapses to what exists. SELF — a 1px edge-control outline inside the row and the trailing word 'You'. DEACTIVATED — name in ink-3, 'No longer active', no chevron, not tappable. LOADING — a 40dp well tile and two well-filled rules. UNRESOLVED — 'Unknown person' with the mono id beneath, tappable to 'Ask your manager who this is'.
items.behaviour: Tap opens whatever the person owns in context, never a profile page that does not exist. Long-press copies the id with a 44dp confirmation — the one legitimate use for a raw id, and a deliberate gesture rather than a permanent display.
items.modes: Night: tile well #141D27, meta #A79E8C. Day: tile #E2DBCC, meta #676052. Veld: 44dp tile with a 2px #1B2632 border, name 18/600, meta 14/600 #4A4437, the mono id at 14/500 — Veld has no text token under 9:1, so even the id clears it.
items.accessibility: One node: 'Thandi Mokoena, field agent at Kasi Corner Spaza.' The no-name case reads 'Field agent at Kasi Corner Spaza, identifier a-b-c-1-2-3', with the id spelled character by character. The initials tile is ExcludeSemantics.
items.amber: None.
items.screenshot: A row with a small rounded square holding 'TM' in bold, then 'Thandi Mokoena' over 'Field agent · Kasi Corner Spaza' in grey, with a thin chevron at the right.

items.name: Progress-to-reward bar
items.purpose: Show how close the agent is to the thing they actually get, in a way that stays honest when the points haven't synced.
items.anatomy: Above the bar, on one baseline in a Wrap: '1 840' in JetBrains Mono figure.l 32/600 and 'of 2 000 points' at title.m 16/600 ink-2. 12dp. The bar: full gutter width, 8dp tall (12dp at 2.0×), radius 4. Track: Night lifted #2C3B4D, Day well #E2DBCC, Veld white with a 2px #1B2632 border. Fill: chart-neutral #8B8271 / ink-3 #676052 / solid #1B2632 — progress, not a verdict, so never mint and never amber. The target: a 2px tick breaking the track's top edge by 2dp, scaling fully with textScaler. 12dp. Below, always, at label 13/500 ink-2: '160 points to the next reward · R 250 airtime'. Never the bar alone.
items.states: IN PROGRESS. REWARD REACHED — the fill goes good, a 10dp filled circle sits at the tick, and the line reads 'Reward reached — R 250 airtime, paid with your next cycle.' Nothing flashes and nothing confettis; an agent in a shop with a customer watching does not want a celebration. NO TARGET SET — the bar does not render at all and a body line says so; an empty bar reads as zero progress, which is a different and false statement. UNKNOWN / OFFLINE — the track renders HATCHED, the figure is an em dash, and the line reads 'Points update when your work sends.' OVERSHOT — the fill runs to 100% and the words carry the surplus. LOADING — a well-filled block at the bar's exact geometry.
items.behaviour: The fill animates once, 600ms on the enter curve, and only when the value actually changed since the last view, so re-opening is not a re-celebration. Instant under reduce-motion, battery-saver and Veld. The tick never moves.
items.modes: Night: track #2C3B4D, fill #8B8271, tick 2px flame-600 — the screen's one amber object. Day: track #E2DBCC, fill #676052, tick 2px #1B2632. Veld: white track with a 2px border, solid #1B2632 fill, a 3px tick with the same 2dp break, figure 34/600, words 16/600.
items.accessibility: 'Progress to reward: 1 840 of 2 000 points. 160 points to the next reward, R 250 airtime.' Hatched reads 'Progress unknown — points update when your work sends.' PARTLY KEPT AGAINST THE CRITIQUE: the tick scales fully with textScaler, but the TRACK scales at half rate, 8→12dp, not 8→16 — a 16dp track is a slab rather than a rule, and the meaning in this component lives in the tick and the sentence, both of which do scale fully.
items.amber: One in Night (the target tick). Zero in Day and Veld.
items.screenshot: '1 840' in large monospaced digits beside 'of 2 000 points', over a slim track mostly filled in warm grey, with a short amber tick standing proud of the track's top edge near the right end, and '160 points to the next reward · R 250 airtime' beneath.

items.name: Live outbox row
items.purpose: One queued capture, alive — what it is, roughly how big it is, what it is doing, and when it will try again.
items.anatomy: Soft row, 64dp min, separated by the tappable-row rule at 3:1, TAPPABLE. Leading 28dp radius-6 glyph tile. 12dp. Text column: label at title.m 16/600 in the agent's words, never the entity type — 'Stock count', 'Submitted visit', 'Photo'; beneath, meta 12 ink-3 with the outlet and time, figures in mono. Trailing, right-aligned: the state word at 11/700 over the payload size in mono 12 ink-3 — REVISED to read 'about 1,4 MB', and to be the DECODED byte size rather than the stored base64 length, which overstates a photo by ~33%. The figure exists so an agent on a 1 GB bundle can decide whether to send now; a number that is wrong in the direction that matters is worse than no number, and 'about' is the honest hedge.
items.states: QUEUED — filled square, 'WAITING', 'queued 07:58'. SENDING — three Oatmeal dots travelling in the tile, 'SENDING', 'sending — 0,9 of 1,4 MB', plus a 2dp determinate rule along the row's bottom edge in chart-neutral. RETRYING — square with a circular arrow, 'RETRYING', and the clock time in mono: 'next try 14:20'. Under reduce-motion nothing moves and the time is the entire signal. STUCK — 1px bad outline tile, half-filled triangle, a 3px bad left bar, 'NEEDS YOU', and the reason in plain words from the stored error code. SENT — mint outline, filled circle, 'SENT', still tappable. WAITING FOR ITS VISIT — 'waiting for the visit to send first', explicitly NOT stuck, because that is an ordering dependency. PRESSED — fill raised.
items.behaviour: Tap opens a sheet: the label as title.l, the reason as body, a mono.ident block with entity type, attempts and last attempt, and actions by state — Queued/Retrying get 'Send this one now' and 'Stop trying'; Stuck gets the one fix as the amber block (tooLarge → 'Shrink the photo and retry'; signedOut → 'Sign in'; rejected → 'Send to support' plus 'Delete this capture' behind a second step); Sent gets 'Sent 08:04 · nothing to do.' A row never auto-deletes and a stuck row stays until the agent acts. The dots and the progress rule are subscribers on the one application Ticker.
items.modes: Night: tile well #141D27, stuck #FF7D8C, size ink-3 #A79E8C. Day: well #E2DBCC, stuck #8C1B2C. Veld: 72dp row, 2px tile border, label 18/600, state word 13/700, and STUCK becomes a solid #7A0F22 tile with a white triangle plus a 4px left bar.
items.accessibility: State first: 'Needs you. Photo, Kasi Corner. Too big to send. Double-tap to fix.' Sending is a liveRegion announcing only on state change, never per byte. The size is announced as 'about one point four megabytes'. Shape carries state in greyscale and scales at 2.0×.
items.amber: None on the row — a queue is a status list. At most one in the sheet it opens: the single fix.
items.screenshot: A row with a small outlined square holding a circular-arrow glyph, 'Photo' in bold, 'Kasi Corner · 07:58' beneath, and on the right 'RETRYING' in small caps over 'about 1,4 MB' in monospaced digits, with 'next try 14:20' under the outlet line.

items.name: Empty state grammar
items.purpose: An empty screen that names the next physical action instead of the absence.
items.anatomy: Left-aligned to the gutter, never centred. A 64px 2px-stroke line drawing in edge-control — a map, a shelf, a box — never an emoji, never an illustration with a mood. 24dp. Headline at display 40/600/1.00 ink-1. 12dp. One body line at 15/400/1.50 ink-2, max 32em, naming what to do in the world. 24dp. One secondary button, 56dp, left-aligned at its natural width. DISPLAY FITTING RULE, NEW — display prose was the one type role with no fitting rule while hero.figure had one keyed to glyph count. Display is now keyed to LINE COUNT after layout: 1–2 lines stay at 40/600, 3 lines step to 32/600, 4 or more to 26/600, floor 26. An Afrikaans headline at 2.0× therefore has a defined shape instead of eating the screen.
items.states: NOTHING YET (first use). NOTHING TODAY — a distinct, recurring state, because 'no route today' is a fact about the plan, not about the agent. FILTERED TO NOTHING — the headline names the filter and the button clears it. NOTHING BECAUSE OFFLINE — never an empty state; it is a held state with whatever is on the phone rendered plus a square-glyph line. ERROR — never an empty state either; it keeps its own grammar with a retry and a statement of what survived.
items.behaviour: No animation. An empty state that animates is asking for attention it has not earned. The button is the only interactive element and it is the actual next step, not 'Refresh'.
items.modes: Night: drawing #7C93AC, headline #EEE9DF, body #C9C1B1. Day: #6E6657, #1B2632, #4A4437. Veld: drawing at 3px stroke, headline 40/700 under the same fitting rule, body 17/600, button 64dp with a 2px border.
items.accessibility: The drawing is ExcludeSemantics. The headline is a Semantics header. Reading order is headline, body, button, and the button's label is a verb phrase, never 'OK'.
items.amber: None. An empty screen has no expected next move strong enough to spend the budget on; the action is a ghost.
items.screenshot: Hard against the left margin: a thin outlined map glyph, 'No route today' in large type, one grey sentence, and a small outlined button reading 'Pick a store to visit'.

items.name: Skeleton grammar
items.purpose: Show the shape of what is coming without lying that it is live.
items.anatomy: Static blocks at the well fill, in the EXACT geometry of the content that will replace them — a 64dp row becomes a 28dp tile plus a 160×16 block plus a 100×12 block, at the real positions. One 1px rule wherever the real separator will be. No rounded pill placeholders that match nothing. After 600ms, and only then, a single 2px OATMEAL rule travels the top edge at 1400ms linear.
items.states: UNDER 600ms — nothing at all; a skeleton that flashes for 200ms is worse than a blank frame. 600ms–8s — the skeleton with its travelling rule. OVER 8s — the rule stops and a 44dp line appears: 'Still loading. This can be slow on a weak signal.' plus a 44dp ghost 'Try again'. FAILED — replaced by the error grammar, never left spinning. PARTIAL — sections that have arrived render for real while the rest stay skeleton.
items.behaviour: The travelling rule is one of the three Ticker subscribers and is killed by reduce-motion, battery-saver and Veld. It is OATMEAL, not amber: a breathing amber means 'happening right now' and a loading placeholder is not live data.
items.modes: Night: blocks well #141D27, rule Oatmeal #C9C1B1. Day: blocks #E2DBCC, rule #4A4437. Veld: NO skeleton at all — the word 'Loading' at 17/600 in #0E141A at the gutter and nothing else, because a grey block field on white at 40% backlight is indistinguishable from a broken screen.
items.accessibility: The region is Semantics(liveRegion:true, label:'Loading') with its child blocks ExcludeSemantics, so a reader hears 'Loading', not eleven empty boxes. The 8s line is announced when it appears.
items.amber: None, by named prohibition.
items.screenshot: Four ghosted rows of flat grey blocks in the exact shape of a list, with a single thin oatmeal line sliding slowly across the top of the group.

items.name: Bottom sheet
items.purpose: Ask something, or explain something, without taking the agent off the screen they are working on.
items.anatomy: Radius 14 top corners only, surface fill, 1px edge-structure outline, a 40×4 grabber in Oatmeal@40% centred 12dp from the top. Scrim: ground at 72%, NO blur (zero BackdropFilter in the app). Padding: gutter 20, 24 top under the grabber, 24 plus safe area at the bottom. Max height 88%; content scrolls inside while the action row stays pinned. Actions are a Column: primary 56dp, 8dp, ghost 56dp — never a side-by-side pair of equal buttons, which is how a destructive choice gets tapped by accident.
items.states: OPEN. SCROLLED (the grabber stays; a 1px rule appears under the title once content scrolls beneath it). DISMISSIBLE (drag, scrim tap, back). NON-DISMISSIBLE (session-ended, first appearance — the scrim ignores taps, back is consumed, the grabber is hidden so the affordance does not lie). TWO-STEP (a destructive confirm cross-fades the sheet's content over 200ms rather than stacking a second sheet). KEYBOARD OPEN (the sheet lifts; the action row rides above it). LOADING (skeleton). ERROR (the sheet STAYS OPEN with a bad-outlined line above the actions; a sheet that closes on failure has thrown the agent's input away).
items.behaviour: Enter 320ms from +24dp; exit 200ms. Drag-to-dismiss follows the finger with a rubber-band. No blur means the sheet is cheap: a ColoredBox with a rim.
items.modes: Night: surface #1B2632, edge-structure #5A7088 (3.00:1 on the fill), scrim #0B1017@72%. Day: #FAF7F2, edge #857C6B (3.86:1), scrim #1B2632@72%, one sh3. Veld: white, radius 0, 2px #1B2632 on all four sides, scrim a solid #1B2632 at 90%, actions 64dp.
items.accessibility: Focus moves in on open and returns to the opening control on close. Semantics(scopesRoute:true, namesRoute:true) with the title as the route name. The grabber carries 'Drag down to close' and is hidden entirely when the sheet is non-dismissible.
items.amber: At most one: the sheet's own primary action, and only when it is the expected next move. A sheet that only explains has none.
items.screenshot: The lower two-thirds of the screen covered by a panel with rounded top corners, a fine rim, a small grabber, the store list dimmed behind it, a heading, three tall option rows, and two stacked buttons — the upper one amber.

items.name: Today / route
items.purpose: Answers the only question that matters at 06:30 — where am I going, and how much is left.
items.anatomy: Header 96dp: 'Today', subtitle meta 12 ink-3, sync chip right. BODY (gutter 20): (1) DAY BLOCK — a standalone soft surface, radius 14, padding 16, REVISED to carry a 1px edge-structure rim (Night surface #1B2632 with a #5A7088 rim, 3.00:1 on the fill and 3.73:1 on the ground; Day #FAF7F2 with #857C6B, 3.86/3.41): eyebrow 'ROUTE'; on one baseline in a Wrap, '4' in mono display 40/600 and 'of 11 stores' at title.m; 12dp; a 6dp progress rule turning good when the route is done; 8dp; '7 left' / 'Route done' at 13/500 — never the bar alone. (2) 32dp. (3) SECTION RULE — a 1px hairline with 'Next up' knocked out on it at title.m; this is the section marker everywhere, and there is no uppercase eyebrow doing that job. (4) NEXT-UP ROW — a standalone soft surface, min 136dp: the sequence in mono 16/500, the distance in mono 13, any flag chips; the outlet name at title.l 20/600 wrapping to 2; the code in mono.ident plus type and last visit; then a 56dp 'Check in here' — the screen's amber. (5) 32dp. (6) SECTION RULE 'Rest of the day'. (7) STOP ROWS — 64dp, separated by the 3:1 tappable rule: a 28dp tile with the sequence in mono, a tick when done, or a hatched tile when skipped; name at title.m; code in mono.ident; right, distance over a state word. (8) A 64dp ghost row 'Visit a store that isn't on the plan', deliberately duplicating the nav circle because a circle is not discoverable. BOTTOM: the tab-root floating row — skin cycle, pill, circle — and no separate thumb zone.
items.states: LOADING (skeleton). NO PLAN AT ALL (empty grammar: 'No route today'). PLAN WITH ZERO STOPS (distinct copy: 'Your plan is empty'). LOAD ERROR (the cached route renders with a square-glyph line; with no cache, the error grammar). ROUTE DONE (the rule goes good, the Next-up section disappears rather than showing an empty card, and the nav circle ARMS). ALL REMAINING SKIPPED (a 44dp line, '4 stores skipped · tap to see why'). NEXT STOP 40 km AWAY (the distance renders with no judgement). 25+ STOPS (ListView.builder; the compact formatter). OFFLINE (identical; only the sync chip changes). 2.0× (the day block's figure and unit stack; Next-up grows to ~200dp; stop rows to ~96dp).
items.behaviour: Pull-to-refresh. Tapping the Next-up row or its button both start check-in; tapping a later stop starts check-in there too — the plan is a plan, not a cage. REVISED: no per-push stagger; the only stagger in the app is this list on first app open. A stop completing while the screen is open re-sorts with a 320ms move.
items.modes: Day (agent default): ground #EEE9DF, day block #FAF7F2 with a 1px #857C6B rim and sh1, 'Check in here' a solid #FFB162 with #1B2632 ink, nav pill solid #2C3B4D. Night: ground #0B1017, day block #1B2632 with a 1px #5A7088 rim, 'Check in here' lifted with a 1px amber rim and a top bleed, nav pill #FFB162. Veld: white, gutter 24, block gap 40, every surface a 2px #1B2632 border at radius 0, rows 64dp with 2px rules, 'Check in here' a 64dp amber block at 18/700, nav pill a solid #1B2632 with white ink.
items.accessibility: Day block is one node: 'Route: 4 of 11 stores done, 7 left.' Each stop row is one node ending in its verb. Section rules are headers. Progress is never colour-only. At 2.0× nothing is pinned and only the outlet name truncates, middle-truncated so the branch survives.
items.amber: Day and Veld: 1 — 'Check in here'; the nav pill is an ink block. Night: 2 — 'Check in here' (rim plus bleed, one object) and the active nav pill. Counted in the composed frame.
items.screenshot: Warm paper. 'Today' top-left, '12 held on this phone' at the right. A soft off-white block with a fine rim: 'ROUTE', '4' huge beside 'of 11 stores', a dark progress rule, '7 left'. A hairline carrying 'Next up'. A taller block: '03 · 1,2 km', 'Kasi Corner Spaza', 'KC-0412 · Spaza · last visit 12 Aug', and a wide amber 'Check in here'. Then 'Rest of the day' and a quiet ruled list.

items.name: Check-in — locating
items.purpose: Wait for a GPS fix in a way that says 'we are looking for you', not 'something is happening'.
items.anatomy: Header 96dp with the outlet name and its code in mono.ident. Body, left-aligned: a 120dp radar block at the gutter; 24dp; 'Finding you' at display 40/600 under the line-count fitting rule; 12dp; 'You need to be within 50 m of the shop. This usually takes a few seconds.' at 15/400/1.50, max 32em, with '50 m' in mono. Thumb zone: skin cycle plus a ghost 'Back to route' — there is no primary action while waiting and the zone does not pretend there is. RADAR: two 1.5px rings expanding 40→120dp over 1800ms, half a cycle apart, with a 2px-stroke 40px pin at the centre.
items.states: UNDER 12s — as above. 12s — a meta line appends: 'Still looking. A tin roof or a fridge aisle can block GPS — step toward the door.' 25s — the rings stop, the pin goes ink-3, and two ghosts appear: 'Try again' and "I can't get closer", which opens the skip-reason picker. There is never a 'check in without GPS'. PERMISSION NEVER ASKED / DENIED MID-WAIT — this state is skipped and the no-GPS screen shows. RESOLVED — the success transition. REDUCE-MOTION / BATTERY-SAVER / VELD — no rings; a static pin and the headline carry the whole message.
items.behaviour: The radar is a local AnimationController, not the shared Ticker — it is full-screen, short-lived and exclusive — and is disposed the instant a result arrives. The screen ALWAYS leaves this state: a throw inside the post-frame check-in call is caught and routed to the 'something else' screen, because the alternative is a radar spinning after the app has stopped looking.
items.modes: Night: the LEADING ring is a single 2px flame-600 stroke (one amber object, emitted light), the trailing ring chart-neutral #8B8271, the pin flame-700 #FFCB94 (12.92:1). Day: both rings ink-1 at decreasing alpha, pin ink-1 — no amber, because the light source outside is the sun. Veld: no radar, no motion; a static 64px 3px-stroke pin-in-a-circle in #1B2632, headline 40/700, body 17/600.
items.accessibility: The screen is Semantics(liveRegion:true) announcing 'Finding you' on entry and 'Still looking' at 12s. The radar is ExcludeSemantics. With no primary action, the reader's last stop is 'Back to route', a real escape. Nothing here depends on motion to be understood.
items.amber: Night 1 (the leading ring). Day and Veld 0.
items.screenshot: Left-aligned on near-black: two faint concentric circles, the outer a thin warm amber, with a small amber pin at their centre; beneath, 'Finding you' large in off-white and one grey sentence about being within 50 m.

items.name: Check-in — success
items.purpose: Land the fact that the visit has started, without spending a screen on it.
items.anatomy: Not a screen — a 320ms transition. The radar collapses to a 28dp filled circle in good, Buzz.done fires, and the visit hub slides up from +24dp. A 44dp line sits under the hub's header for 6 seconds: a 12dp filled circle in good, then 'Checked in 07:42 · inside the fence' at 13/500 ink-2, time in mono. The line fades over 200ms — a receipt, not a banner.
items.states: INSIDE THE FENCE. INSIDE BUT MARGINAL (accuracy worse than 30 m): 'Checked in 07:42 · GPS is rough here (±45 m)', and a neutral 'Out of fence' chip is NOT added — an uncertain fix is not an accusation. Accuracy is recorded either way. RE-CHECK-IN after a resume: 'Checked in again 09:10 · your earlier work is still here.' REDUCE-MOTION / VELD: no collapse; the hub appears and the line is present from the first frame, staying 10 seconds rather than 6 because there was no motion to carry the moment.
items.behaviour: Buzz.done — heavier than a tick, because the agent is about to stop looking at the phone and start looking at the shelf. REVISED: no children stagger behind it; the hub arrives whole. The line is dismissible by tap, never blocks the hub, and never shifts its layout.
items.modes: Night: circle in good #6FE0AE (11.76:1), line ink-2 over the well. Day: good #14664A, ink-2 #4A4437. Veld: no fade, no collapse; a solid #0F5039 block, 56dp, white ink at 16/600, dismissed by tap only.
items.accessibility: A liveRegion announcing 'Checked in at Kasi Corner Spaza, 07:42, inside the fence' once. Focus moves to the hub's first section row, not to the receipt. Nothing about the success depends on the green.
items.amber: None. Success is a status.
items.screenshot: The visit hub with a slim line under the header: a small green dot and 'Checked in 07:42 · inside the fence' in oatmeal.

items.name: Check-in failure — too far
items.purpose: Say how far away the agent actually is, how well we know it, and be honest about what retrying from the car park actually costs.
items.anatomy: Left-aligned. Header with outlet name and code. BODY: eyebrow 'CHECK-IN'; 12dp; headline display 40/600 (line-count fitting rule), 'You are too far from the shop.'; 24dp; THE MEASURED DISTANCE as the hero — a standalone soft surface with a 1px rim, radius 14, padding 16, carrying a 3px bad left bar at full height and a filled triangle before its eyebrow: '180 m' in mono hero.figure.compact 56/600 ink-1, then at 15/400 ink-2 'You need to be within 50 m. Right now you are 180 m away.' REVISED, and this is the honesty fix: whenever horizontal accuracy exceeds 30 m the hero line reads '180 m · GPS is rough here (±40 m)' in the same mono voice the success receipt already uses. The screen that penalises the agent was being less honest about measurement error than the screen that congratulates them. 24dp; then the attempts note. THUMB ZONE: 'Try again' amber; ghost 'Back to route'; and, always present, a ghost "I can't get closer" opening the skip-reason picker.
items.states: FIRST AND SECOND ATTEMPT — the note reads 'Every attempt is recorded with where you were.' REVISED: the sentence 'Trying again from far away counts against this visit' is NOT shown here, because the penalty does not start here. THIRD AND BEYOND — the penalty sentence appears at the same moment the primary DEMOTES to a ghost and "I can't get closer" PROMOTES to the amber block, so the warning and the consequence arrive together; the app stops encouraging the behaviour it is about to penalise. UNDER 80 m — 'You're close. Try walking to the front door.' OVER 2 km — 'This looks like the wrong store, or the store's pin is wrong.' plus a ghost 'The pin is wrong' that queues a correction. MOVING — REVISED: the figure updates only on a fix whose accuracy improved or whose change exceeds the accuracy radius, and 'getting closer' appears only after three consecutive monotonic fixes. A metre-precise figure animating on ±40 m urban noise, beside a sentence saying that figure is held against you, was the worst thing on this screen. OFFLINE — identical; the geofence is computed on device.
items.behaviour: Retry re-runs the whole check-in, returning to the locating state. The figure counts to its new value rather than resetting. Buzz is a single tick on retry, never a failure buzz — the agent already knows.
items.modes: Night: bad #FF7D8C for the bar and triangle, the figure in ink-1 (a severity-coded figure is never amber and never the severity hue at 56px), 'Try again' lifted with an amber rim. Day: bad #8C1B2C, figure #1B2632, 'Try again' a solid amber block. Veld: the block's fill goes and a 2px border arrives, the left bar becomes 4px #7A0F22, the figure 56/700, body 17/600, 'Try again' a 64dp amber block at 18/700.
items.accessibility: Announced as 'Too far from the shop. You are 180 metres away, give or take 40. You need to be within 50 metres.' The figure carries an explicit semanticsLabel spelling the unit. Severity is a bar, a triangle and a sentence — never the hue. All three actions ≥56dp.
items.amber: 1 — 'Try again', or from the third attempt "I can't get closer". Never both.
items.screenshot: Near-black, left-aligned: 'CHECK-IN' small, 'You are too far from the shop.' large, a soft panel with a fine rim and a crimson bar down its left edge holding '180 m' in huge monospaced digits with '· GPS is rough here (±40 m)' beside it, a grey note that attempts are recorded, and a dark button with a thin amber rim reading 'Try again'.

items.name: Check-in failure — no GPS
items.purpose: Distinguish 'your phone cannot see the sky' from 'you are in the wrong place', and hand over the actual fix.
items.anatomy: Left-aligned. Header with outlet name and code. BODY: a 64px 2px-stroke satellite-with-a-slash in edge-control; 24dp; headline display 40/600 under the fitting rule, "Your phone can't find where you are."; 12dp; the specific reason from the location service in plain words; 12dp; the fix in one line; 24dp; 'Nothing is lost — you have not captured anything yet.' THUMB ZONE: amber 'Open settings' (a real deep link, because 'go to settings' with no link is an instruction, not a fix); ghost 'Try again'; ghost 'Back to route'.
items.states: SWITCHED OFF — the link targets location settings. PERMISSION DENIED — it targets the app's permission page and the body adds 'You can allow it just while using the app.' DENIED FOREVER — 'Try again' is removed because it cannot succeed. NO FIX YET — 'Open settings' is replaced by an amber 'Try again' and the body reads 'Step outside or near a window and try again.' AIRPLANE MODE — named explicitly: 'Your GPS still works in airplane mode — give it a few seconds.' MOCK LOCATION — a distinct, non-accusatory screen: 'Your phone is reporting a fake location. Turn off any location-spoofing app to check in.', with no retry until the setting changes. RETURNING FROM SETTINGS — the app re-checks on resume and moves straight to locating without another tap.
items.behaviour: On resume the permission and service state is re-read and the screen self-corrects rather than waiting for a tap. No spinner: retry goes to the locating state. Never red — this is a missing capability, not a severity, and the glyph is a line drawing rather than a warning triangle.
items.modes: Night: drawing #7C93AC, 'Open settings' lifted with an amber rim. Day: drawing #6E6657, a solid amber block. Veld: drawing at 3px, headline 40/700, body 17/600, all three actions 64dp with 2px borders, amber on the primary only.
items.accessibility: Announced as 'Your phone cannot find where you are. Location is switched off.' The drawing is ExcludeSemantics. Each action label is a verb phrase. Reason and fix are separate paragraphs so a reader can get the fix without re-hearing the diagnosis.
items.amber: 1 — the primary, whichever it is for the specific cause.
items.screenshot: Left-aligned on warm paper: a thin outlined satellite with a slash, "Your phone can't find where you are." large, two grey sentences, a wide amber 'Open settings' and an outlined 'Try again' beneath.

items.name: Check-in failure — something else
items.purpose: Say the app failed, not that the agent did — and make the failure reportable.
items.anatomy: Left-aligned. Header with outlet name and code. BODY: a 64px 2px-stroke broken link; 24dp; headline display 40/600, "We couldn't start the visit."; 12dp; the humanised message at 15/400 — never a stack trace; 16dp; a well-filled block, radius 10, padding 12, with a 1px rim, holding the error code in mono.ident 13/500 ('checkin/db-locked · 07:41') and a 44dp ghost 'Copy', because the one thing an agent can do for a failure they cannot fix is tell someone precisely; 24dp; 'Nothing was lost — you had not captured anything yet.' That sentence is the difference between retrying and giving up on the shop. THUMB ZONE: amber 'Try again'; ghost 'Back to route'.
items.states: FIRST FAILURE. REPEATED (3+) — a 44dp ghost 'Tell your manager' opens a pre-filled message carrying the code, outlet and time. STORAGE FULL — 'Your phone is out of space. Free some up, then try again.' plus a ghost to storage settings. DATABASE LOCKED — 'Another copy of TradeIQ may be running. Close it and try again.' UNKNOWN — the generic body plus the code. OFFLINE — never shown; check-in is local and offline is not a failure.
items.behaviour: Retry resets the whole check-in state machine including the started flag, so the post-frame call actually fires again. The code block is selectable and copyable. No auto-retry loop — an app that silently retries a failing local write burns battery and tells the agent nothing.
items.modes: Night: drawing #7C93AC, code block on the well with a #5A7088 rim. Day: #6E6657 and #E2DBCC. Veld: drawing 3px, the code block loses its fill and takes a 2px border, code at 14/500 — Veld has no text token under 9:1, including a machine code.
items.accessibility: Announced as "We couldn't start the visit", then the humanised reason, then 'Nothing was lost'. The code is spelled character by character. 'Copy' carries 'Copy the error code'.
items.amber: 1 — 'Try again'.
items.screenshot: A thin outlined broken-chain glyph, "We couldn't start the visit." large, a grey explanation, a small recessed strip holding 'checkin/db-locked · 07:41' in monospaced grey with a tiny Copy button, and a reassurance line over an amber 'Try again'.

items.name: Visit hub
items.purpose: One place that shows what has been captured, what is left, and why the submit is still closed — with no tabs, because mid-visit navigation loses work.
items.anatomy: Header 96dp, capped: outlet name at title.l wrapping to 2; subtitle at 13/400 ink-2, max 2 lines then tail-truncated; sync chip right; flag chips in a Wrap of at most 2 rows with an 'and N more' expander. BODY (gutter 20): (1) READINESS BLOCK — a standalone soft surface with a 1px edge-structure rim (Night #1B2632 + #5A7088; Day #FAF7F2 + #857C6B), radius 14, padding 16: eyebrow 'CAPTURED'; on one baseline in a Wrap, '5' in mono figure.l 32/600 and '/8' at 22/600 ink-3; to the right, wrapping under at 2.0×, the readiness in WORDS — 'Ready to submit' with a filled circle, or '3 sections still needed' with a 1px bad outline and a half-filled triangle. 12dp. A 6dp rule with a 2px target tick at the required-sections mark, breaking the track's top edge. (2) 32dp. (3) A 13/500 line ABOVE the ladder, promoted from meta at the bottom: 'Do them in any order. Everything saves as you go.' (4) SECTION RULE 'Sections'. (5) THE LADDER — full-width soft rows, 64dp min, separated by the 3:1 tappable rule, NOT a tile grid and REVISED to drop the 2px rule that wired the tiles together: 28dp state glyph tile, name at title.m wrapping to 2, detail at meta 12 with figures in mono, a REQUIRED badge under the name when required and not done, and right, '6/6' in mono or an 18dp chevron. (6) THE SCORE ROW last: a hatched tile with an em dash, 'Score' in ink-2, 'Worked out when the visit sends', no chevron, not tappable — and NOT at reduced opacity. THUMB ZONE: skin cycle plus 'Submit this visit'; when blocked, a BarNote above naming every blocker by name, wrapping, never truncated.
items.states: LOADING (skeleton). READ FAILED (the chrome renders; the ladder becomes an error line with a retry and submit stays disabled). BLOCKED (submit disabled, the BarNote names the blockers). READY (submit becomes the amber block; the rule goes good). PARTIAL SECTION (half-disc glyph plus its count). CAN'T-CONFIRM SECTION (hatched tile; it stops blocking and the readiness line reads '5 captured · 1 can't confirm'). ALL REQUIRED SECTIONS CAN'T-CONFIRM — NEW: the submit changes identity entirely to 'Record this as a store I could not work' and the readiness line reads '0 captured · 7 not confirmed'; see the submit gate. NO CLIENT TEMPLATE (that row is absent and the count changes). OFFLINE (identical — progress derives from the local outbox, which is why it survives the app being killed). APP KILLED AND REOPENED (rebuilt from the outbox). 2.0× (rows to ~104dp; the readiness Wrap drops the word under the figure; the header scrolls once it passes 40% of the viewport).
items.behaviour: Tapping a row pushes the section full-screen from the right, 320ms, with no stagger behind it. Returning re-derives progress from the outbox stream. Submit opens the gate screen — never submits directly, because this is the moment the agent accuses a store of something.
items.modes: Day: ground #EEE9DF, readiness block #FAF7F2 with a #857C6B rim and sh1, rule fill #676052 on #E2DBCC, good #14664A, bad #8C1B2C. Night: ground #0B1017, block #1B2632 with a #5A7088 rim, fill #8B8271 on #2C3B4D, good #6FE0AE, bad #FF7D8C, submit lifted with an amber rim. Veld: white, gutter 24, block gap 40, the block a 2px-bordered rectangle at radius 0, rows 64dp with 2px rules, name 18/600, detail 14/600, REQUIRED a solid #7A0F22 with white ink, submit a 64dp amber block at 18/700.
items.accessibility: Readiness is one node: 'Captured, 5 of 8. 3 sections still needed.' Each row is one node ending in its verb. The score row announces 'Score, not yet available' and is not focusable as a button. The disabled submit keeps its label and appends the blockers.

A soft block with a fine rim: 'CAPTURED', '5' big beside '/8', '3 sections still needed' with a small outlined triangle. A line reading 'Do them in any order.' Then a hairline 'Sections' and a column of separate small squares — two green ticks, one half-disc, one striped, three empty — each beside a section name, a grey detail line, and one crimson-outlined 'REQUIRED'.

items.name: Section form grammar
items.purpose: One grammar that builds all the capture sections, so an agent who learns one learns them all — and so nobody ever designs another screen.
items.anatomy: Header 96dp: the section name, subtitle 'Saves as you go'. BODY (gutter 20) is a stack of FIELD GROUPS: an optional group rule (a 1px hairline with a title.m label knocked out), fields 16dp apart, 32dp between groups. Exactly EIGHT primitives, and every section is built only from these: (a) COUNT FIELD — label above, then the stepper. (b) NUMBER / TEXT — the trough. (c) CHOICE ROW — 2–4 chips, 48dp (Veld 56), radius 6, 1px edge-control, wrapping to two rows rather than scrolling horizontally; selected takes a fill plus a 2px-stroke tick plus weight 700. (d) TOGGLE — a 52×32 track with a 28dp thumb AND the state word; the word is not optional. (e) CHECK LIST — a 28dp box (48 at 2.0×), the whole 64dp row the target. (f) NOTE — 3 lines, counter past 80%. (g) REPEATING CARD SET — each entry a standalone soft surface with a 1px rim, a 40dp header row with the entry name and a 48dp remove control with a real semanticLabel, and a 64dp ghost 'Add another'; entries numbered in mono ('2 of 3'), never '01/02/03'. (h) PHOTO FIELD. FOOTER, identical everywhere: a 56dp inline 'Save' — the only thing that persists — and beneath it a 64dp ghost "Can't confirm this section" opening the skip-reason picker. THUMB ZONE: skin cycle plus 'Save and go back'.
items.states: UNTOUCHED. DIRTY (Save becomes the amber block; before any change it is a ghost, so a section needing no edit is not nagging). SAVING (three Oatmeal dots). SAVED (a 44dp line: square glyph, 'Saved on this phone · 07:58'; Buzz.tick). SAVE FAILED (values untouched: 'Not saved. Your answers are still here — try Save again.'). PARTIALLY SAVED ('Saved 7 of 12'). CAN'T CONFIRM (the body dims to ink-2 and locks, a hatched 44dp line names the reason, and a ghost 'I can confirm it after all' unlocks it). LEAVING DIRTY (a 3-row sheet: amber 'Save and go back', ghost 'Go back without saving', ghost 'Stay here' — never a two-button dialog where 'Discard' sits beside 'Save'). LOADING (skeleton at the real geometry). EMPTY DATA (the empty grammar inside the body, Save hidden). 2.0× (everything grows; nothing is side-by-side except the stepper, which stacks with its ± pair still adjacent).
items.behaviour: Sections can be done in ANY order — a delivery blocking the aisle is why. Fields write to local state on change and to the outbox only on Save. The keyboard pushes the bottom region up; the focused field scrolls to 96dp above it. No section has tabs, a stepper or a 'next section' button: the way out is back to the hub. No stagger on entry.
items.modes: Night: group rules #3A4B60, chips #7C93AC with a selected fill of #2C3B4D and a 1px amber rim, Save lifted with an amber rim flooding on press. Day: rules #DED7C9, selected chip a solid #1B2632 with #EEE9DF ink, Save a solid amber block. Veld: gutter 24, group gap 40, every rule 2px, chips 56dp with 2px borders and a solid #1B2632 selected fill, Save a 64dp amber block at 18/700, body 17/600.
items.accessibility: Each group is a header plus its fields. Every label is bound to its control and re-announced on error. The toggle is Semantics(toggled:) and always pairs with its word. Remove carries 'Remove competitor 2 of 3'. The Save state line is a liveRegion.
items.amber: At most 2 in Night: Save's rim and the one focused input's rule. Day and Veld: exactly 1 — Save.
items.screenshot: A form on warm paper: a hairline carrying 'On shelf', an oatmeal label over a flat-topped trough, three outlined chips with the middle one filled dark and ticked, a toggle with 'Yes' beside it, then a wide amber 'Save' and an outlined "Can't confirm this section".

items.name: Stock counter screen
items.purpose: Count a shelf one-handed, in a dark aisle, where an out-of-stock is the most valuable thing the agent can record — and where a product nobody looked at is never reported as empty.
items.anatomy: Header: 'Stock & availability' / '12 SKUs · saves as you go'. A STICKY 44dp summary rule under the header, not a card: '4 counted · 1 out of stock · 8 to go', figures in mono, with a 1px hairline beneath; past 12 SKUs with any uncounted, a 44dp ghost 'Jump to the first uncounted' appears in it. BODY: one SKU block per product, separated by the 3:1 rule, padding 16 vertical: ROW A — SKU name at title.m wrapping to 2, 'RRP R 24,99' right in mono 13/500 through the locale formatter. ROW B — read-only server context at meta 12, 'selling ~4,2/day · 12 days cover'; with no history it reads 'no sales history yet', never a fabricated 0,0. ROW C — the stepper, trough leading, ± pair trailing. Then the photo field, the inline Save, and "Can't confirm this section".
items.states: NOT COUNTED (em dash plus 'not counted'). COUNTED. ZERO / FINDING — a 3px bad left bar at the block's full height, the figure in bad with a filled triangle, and 'Out of stock. This raises a task for the manager.' plus 'Shoppers switch brands when the shelf is empty.' Buzz.finding. NOT COUNTED AT SAVE — REVISED, and this is the major the critic was most right about. The app must stop writing uncounted as zero. An uncounted SKU now sends NULL: the stepper already has a first-class 'not counted' state and the scorecard already has an unmeasured grammar built for exactly this, so the data model has the shape and only the write was wrong. Saving a part-counted section is an ordinary act — the section's own promise is 'Saves as you go' — and it must not turn eight unlooked-at products into eight accusations against a store. UNTIL THE SERVER TAKES NULL, the 44dp line becomes a blocking two-step sheet: 'Save 4 counts' (amber) versus 'Save 4 counts and record 8 as out of stock' (ghost, consequence named) — the same accusation the submit gate exists to gate, gated the same way. NO SKUs — empty grammar plus a ghost 'Raise it'. 60+ SKUs — ListView.builder, the sticky summary the only fixed chrome. LOADING / LOAD FAILED / SAVE FAILED / PARTIAL SAVE — as the section grammar. 2.0× — the stepper stacks, trough on top, the ± pair adjacent beneath.
items.behaviour: The summary rule is a liveRegion updating on every change. Long-press a step repeats at 8/second after 400ms with a tick every fifth. Tapping the figure opens the number sheet. Buzz.finding on zero is heavier and longer than the tick. Nothing auto-saves; Save is explicit and also queues the optional photo, and a second Save re-sends the counts, not a duplicate photo.

Night: ground #0B1017, trough #141D27, figure #EEE9DF, finding #FF7D8C, focused trough a 2px #FFCB94 rule with a bloom, Save lifted with an amber rim. Veld: gutter 24, stepper 64dp with 2px borders, figure 24/600, name 18/600, context 14/600, the finding a 4px #7A0F22 left bar plus the words with no tint, Save a 64dp amber block.

Not counted announces 'not counted' — never 'zero'. Zero announces 'Zero — out of stock, this raises a task for the manager' first. The stepper exposes increase/decrease actions.
