items.name: Photo capture — Phase 1 pre-capture card
items.purpose: Tell the agent what to shoot and to switch the torch on before the OS camera takes over — the honest version of capture, given there is no camera package in pubspec.
items.anatomy: Header 96dp: the section name, subtitle 'One photo'. BODY (gutter 20): a 96dp FRAMING CARD — a standalone soft surface with a 1px edge-structure rim, radius 14: a 64px 2px-stroke shelf bay with four corner brackets on the left, 16dp, then the framing line at 15/400 ink-1, 'Stand back far enough to get the whole bay, including the price rail.' 16dp. A 48dp TORCH REMINDER ROW, shown when the last capture's mean luma was under 18% or local solar elevation is below 0: a square glyph plus 'Aisle dark? Switch your phone torch on before you shoot.' at 13/500 — and the word TORCH is never an amber block, because calling a torch-on control a light source is a pun, not a rule. 16dp. 'Your photo is stamped with the time and where you are.' THUMB ZONE: skin cycle plus amber 'Open camera'; ghost 'Cancel'.
items.states: DEFAULT. TORCH HINT SHOWN / HIDDEN. PERMISSION DENIED — the card is replaced by the no-permission grammar plus amber 'Open settings'. CAMERA UNAVAILABLE — 'This phone has no camera we can reach.' plus a ghost 'Skip the photo', because the section must remain completable. RETURNING WITH A PHOTO — straight to the review strip; this screen is popped. RETURNING WITH NOTHING — this screen stays unchanged with any existing photo intact; a backed-out retake loses nothing. HANDOFF FAILED — an error line with a humanised reason and a retry, here rather than on a lost route. LOW STORAGE — 'Your phone is nearly full. A photo may not save.'
items.behaviour: 'Open camera' hands off to the OS camera via the existing service; there is no in-app preview in Phase 1 and this screen does not pretend there is. On return a luma-variance check runs on the returned bytes; any frame under 18% mean luma is edged and questioned in the review strip, never auto-rejected, because a dark photo may be the only obtainable evidence during Stage 6.

Veld: the card a 2px-bordered rectangle at radius 0, drawing 3px, framing line 17/600, torch row 56dp at 16/600, 'Open camera' a 64dp amber block at 18/700.
items.accessibility: The drawing is ExcludeSemantics; the framing line carries the whole instruction. The torch row is a liveRegion when it appears. 'Open camera' carries 'Open the camera to photograph the shelf'.
items.amber: 1 — 'Open camera'.
items.screenshot: A soft block with a fine rim holding a thin outlined shelf drawing with corner brackets beside 'Stand back far enough to get the whole bay, including the price rail.' Under it a row with a solid square and 'Aisle dark? Switch your phone torch on before you shoot.' At the bottom, a wide amber 'Open camera'.

items.name: Photo capture — Phase 2 in-app camera
items.purpose: The scoped, funded version: a full-bleed preview with static framing brackets, a first-class torch and a real shutter.
items.anatomy: Full-bleed CameraController preview running NIGHT tokens regardless of skin — it is a camera, it is dark. Four STATIC 2px flame-600 corner brackets with 32px arms, inset 32dp, counted as ONE amber object. A solid abyss-000@70% control strip across the bottom, 128dp, never a blur (BackdropFilter over a live camera texture is a frame killer). On the strip: the last-shot thumb REVISED from 48dp to 56dp so it meets the stated ≥56dp floor the old spec contradicted in its own accessibility line; the SHUTTER centred at 72dp — a 3px flame-600 ring with a 60dp ink-1 disc, the one centred element in the system, because a thumb is centred; a 56dp TORCH control on the right, a filled Abyssal #1B2632 block with a 2px-stroke glyph in ink-1 and the word ON or OFF REVISED from 11/700 to 13/700. A 44dp line above the strip carries the framing hint.
items.states: PREVIEW READY. INITIALISING (the strip is present and the preview area is ground with 'Starting the camera' at body.strong — never a black rectangle). TORCH ON / OFF (the block fills and the word changes; both channels). CAPTURING (the disc shrinks to 48dp over 120ms and the preview freezes for 200ms). SAVING (the thumb shows a well block with three Oatmeal dots). SHOT COUNT (a mono 13 count beside the thumb). PERMISSION DENIED / BUSY / DISCONNECTED (the preview area carries a left-aligned message and a retry; the strip stays so the agent can leave). LOW LIGHT ('Very dark. The torch will help.'; nothing is blocked). STORAGE FULL (capture disabled with the reason named). LIVE SHELF-EDGE DETECTION IS CUT, not deferred — a 30fps YUV edge detector costs 8–15ms/frame on a Snapdragon 4xx — and the old amber→mint bracket snap is gone because those hues are 1.11:1 in true colour and 1.01:1 under deuteranopia.
items.behaviour: Shutter: Buzz.tick, 120ms shrink, 200ms freeze, then the thumb updates. Torch: Buzz.tick, instant. Back exits with whatever has been shot. No pinch-zoom — a zoomed shelf photo is not evidence of a bay. The preview pauses on background and resumes on return.
items.modes: The camera runs Night tokens in all three skins. VELD CONCESSIONS, REVISED to be more than size: the strip goes to 144dp, the shutter to 80dp, the torch to 64dp, and — the fix the critic asked for — the torch's state word goes to Veld's own label scale, 16/700, because the torch is the exact control the sun-and-dark case turns on and an 11px word on a dark strip was the thing Veld exists to prevent.
items.accessibility: The shutter carries a required semanticLabel 'Take the photo'; the torch is Semantics(toggled:) with 'Torch, off. Double-tap to turn on.'; the thumb is 'Last photo, 3 taken. Double-tap to review.' The brackets are ExcludeSemantics. Every control ≥56dp.

items.name: Photo review strip and viewer
items.purpose: See what was actually captured while the evidence can still be re-taken — and never delete a dark photo that may be the only one obtainable.
items.anatomy: STRIP: 72dp thumbs, radius 10, 8dp gaps, horizontal, inside the section body, each with a 2px border. Up to 6, then a 72dp well tile with '+3' in mono. Under an underexposed thumb, a caption at meta 12 ink-2 'Dark — retake?' and a 44dp ghost 'Retake'. VIEWER (full screen): the photo fit to width, pinch-zoom to 4×; a 44dp mono.ident line at the bottom, '07:52 · geotagged · about 1,4 MB'; thumb zone with a ghost 'Retake' and an amber 'Use it'.
items.states: CAPTURED (2px edge-control border). UNDEREXPOSED, mean luma under 18% (2px comparison border — #E08E71 Night, #A35139 Day — plus the caption; NEVER auto-rejected, never deleted). QUEUED (a 16dp filled-square badge, scaling at 2.0×). SENDING (three travelling dots). SENT (a filled circle in good). STUCK (a half-filled triangle plus a 3px bad left bar; tapping opens the outbox sheet). DECODE FAILED (a well tile with a broken-image glyph and 'This photo did not save. Take it again.' — the section stays saveable without it). GEOTAG MISSING ('no location on this photo' stated in the viewer, not hidden, because the geotag is what places a stock count for the fraud module). ZERO PHOTOS (the strip is absent). LOADING (well tiles).
items.behaviour: Tap opens the viewer, 320ms. 'Retake' re-opens capture and the current photo survives until a new one lands. Images decode with cacheWidth set to devicePixelRatio × logical width — a 12 MP shelf photo decoded full-size is an OOM on a 2 GB handset. No blur, no shadow inside the scrolling strip.

items.name: Submit gate
items.purpose: The one moment the agent accuses a store of something — so it shows exactly what the submission will do, and asks. And it is now the place where a visit with nothing in it stops being a visit.
items.anatomy: Header: 'Submit this visit' / outlet and time in store. BODY (gutter 20): (1) intro at 15/400/1.50 ink-2: 'This is what you are about to tell the manager. Nothing here was added by the app.' (2) 16dp. CAPTURED BLOCK — a standalone soft surface with a 1px rim: a 28dp good tile with a tick, '7 of 8 sections complete' at title.m, and the captured line at meta; when anything is can't-confirm, a second line with a hatched glyph naming it. (3) 32dp. SECTION RULE 'What this raises · 3'. (4) TASK ROWS — 64dp min, separated by the 3:1 rule: a 28dp tile — urgent a solid bad-solid fill with a filled triangle plus a 3px left bar on the row; routine a 1px bad outline with a half-filled triangle; title at 15/600 wrapping freely; beneath, 'Task for the manager · high' at 12/500 — the priority is ALWAYS in the word. (5) REVISED, and this closes the fraud path the critic found: every CAN'T-CONFIRM section now gets its own row here — 'Store refused the stock count — the manager is told' — because a store that refused four sections IS something to raise, and the old design listed nothing. (6) When there is genuinely nothing: a mint-outlined block with a filled circle, 'Nothing to raise. This store is clean.' THUMB ZONE: an offline note where applicable (square glyph, never red), then amber 'Submit this visit', then ghost 'Go back and change something'.
items.states: NORMAL. NO WORKABLE VISIT — NEW and load-bearing: when every REQUIRED section is can't-confirm, or zero sections were captured, the primary is not 'Submit this visit' at all. It becomes 'Record this as a store I could not work', which writes a skipped visit carrying its reasons — a different object to the server and to the fraud module than a submitted visit with no data. The old design let four skip-sheet taps produce a scored visit with nothing in it and a gate printing 'This store is clean', which was the cleanest fraud path in the app. THREE OR MORE CAN'T-CONFIRM — the visit carries a 'sections not confirmed' flag chip that the manager sees. LOADING (skeleton). REVIEW READ FAILED (the gate still submits and says so; the primary is intact). ZERO TASKS (the clean-store block). 12+ TASKS (the list scrolls; the count is in the section rule). OFFLINE (the note; submit is unaffected, because submitting is a local write). SUBMITTING (busy; the back chevron disabled). SUBMITTED (no dialog, no success screen — Buzz.done, then the route REPLACES to the outcome). SUBMIT FAILED LOCALLY (the primary returns, a bad-outlined line names it, nothing is lost). 2.0× (rows to ~104dp).
items.behaviour: Reached only from the hub, never from a tap on a list. The primary is a single tap but it is the second deliberate step — the gate itself is the confirmation, so there is no third dialog. Double-tap protection via busy.

Night: block #1B2632 with a #5A7088 rim, urgent a solid #E23C55 with #0B1017 ink (4.55:1), routine a 1px #FF7D8C outline, submit lifted with an amber rim flooding on press. Veld: gutter 24, block gap 40, the block a 2px-bordered rectangle, rows separated by 2px rules, urgent a solid #7A0F22 plus a 4px left bar, title 18/600, priority 14/600, submit a 64dp amber block at 18/700.
items.accessibility: Each task row announces severity first: 'Urgent. Out of stock on Coke 500ml. Task for the manager, high priority.' A can't-confirm row announces 'Not confirmed. Stock count — the store refused.' The primary's label is the full sentence, so a reader is never asked to confirm 'Submit'. The no-workable-visit primary announces its own different consequence.

items.name: Outcome — scored
items.purpose: The score is the point of the visit, so it is where the visit ends — and it is the number the manager will actually see.
items.anatomy: Header: 'How it went' / the outlet name. BODY (gutter 20), left-aligned: eyebrow 'PERFECT STORE SCORE'; 8dp; the hero in a Wrap — '71' in mono hero.figure 72/600 ink-1, tabular, with '/100' demoted to a 16/500 suffix on its own baseline; beside it, dropping to its own line at 2.0×, the band: a glyph (filled circle / half-filled triangle / filled triangle, scaling with textScaler) plus the word at 13/500 — 'On target' / 'Watch' / 'Below standard'. 12dp. The delta: a SOLID TRIANGLE plus '+6 from your last visit (65)' at 13/600, figures in mono. 32dp. SECTION RULE 'How it was worked out'. Then one row per dimension, 64dp, separated by the tappable-row rule where tappable and the decorative rule where not: name at title.m; the value right in mono 16/600 or an em dash; a 5dp bar beneath — track well, fill chart-neutral, and a 2px target tick breaking the track's top edge. THUMB ZONE: amber 'Next store'; ghost 'See my visits'.
items.states: SCORED. UNMEASURED DIMENSION — the bar is HATCHED, the value an em dash, and a reason line follows: 'No competitor on shelf — nothing to score.' Never a zero, because a zero reads as a failure at something the agent was never given a chance to do. NO PREVIOUS VISIT — no delta, no arrow: 'First scored visit here.' DELTA OF ZERO — a FLAT triangle and 'Same as your last visit (71)'. CHANGED ON REVIEW — the reconciliation line (see its own item). SENT BACK LATER — a 'Sent back' flag chip and the manager's note as a body block. READ-ONLY (from My visits) — the thumb zone becomes the 76dp skin-cycle-only zone with a ghost 'Back'; 'Next store' does not exist outside the live flow. LOADING — skeleton of the hero and six rows. 2.0× — the hero caps at 1.6× (documented in the token, not hidden in a wrapper) and the band, delta and unit each take their own line.
items.behaviour: The figure counts up over 600ms on ease-out-quart — the one moment in the visit worth landing. Instant under reduce-motion, battery-saver and Veld. Bars animate once, 600ms, staggered 40ms — kept here, and only here, because the bars are the explanation of the number and their order is the reading order. The back chevron goes to Today: there is no way back into a submitted visit.

Night: figure #EEE9DF (a severity-coded figure is never amber), good #6FE0AE, bad #FF7D8C, track #2C3B4D, fill #8B8271, tick 2px #FFB162, 'Next store' lifted with an amber rim. Unmeasured: 'Competitive, not measured. No competitor on shelf — nothing to score.' The band never depends on the dot. Hatch survives greyscale, deuteranopia and a sun-washed panel.

items.name: Outcome — held on phone, and scoring
items.purpose: The ordinary case in a shop with no signal: submitted, safe, and not yet scored — a receipt, not an error.
items.anatomy: HELD: header as the scored screen. Body, left-aligned: a 28dp tile with a filled SQUARE glyph, then at title.l 20/600 "Submitted. It's on your phone until you have signal."; 12dp; 'Your captures are safe. They send the moment you have a bar of signal.'; 24dp; SECTION RULE 'Waiting to send'; then the live outbox rows for THIS visit only, so the agent can watch it go rather than trust a sentence; 24dp; the honesty line at meta 12/1.50: "We don't guess your score. You'll see the real one when it sends." THUMB ZONE: amber 'Next store'; ghost 'Open my work'. SCORING: the skeleton of the scored screen at its real geometry with the Oatmeal rule travelling after 600ms.
items.states: HELD — NO SIGNAL. HELD — SERVER UNREACHABLE (the same screen, one line different: 'We could not reach the server. Your captures are safe either way.' Failing to READ a score is not failing to submit). SENDING (the rows go live; when the last lands the screen swaps to scored with a 320ms cross-fade, no reload). PARTIALLY SENT ('3 of 7 sent'). ONE ITEM STUCK (that row takes the stuck state plus a 44dp line, '1 capture needs you before this can be scored.'). SIGNED OUT MID-SEND (the session-ended sheet appears over this screen with the held work visible behind it — the whole point of that sheet being a sheet). SCORING TIMED OUT (after 20s the skeleton resolves to the held state rather than spinning).
items.behaviour: The screen listens to the outbox stream and transitions on its own. The back chevron goes to Today. No number is ever shown here, and that refusal is stated in a sentence rather than left as an absence.
items.modes: Night: square glyph and copy in ink-2 over the well, 'Next store' lifted with an amber rim. Day: ink-2 #4A4437 over #E2DBCC. Veld: the tile 32dp with a 2px border, headline 22/700, body 17/600, honesty line 14/600, 'Next store' a 64dp amber block; no cross-fade — the scored screen simply replaces this one.
items.accessibility: Announced as 'Submitted. Held on this phone until you have signal.' The outbox rows keep their state-first semantics. The honesty line is read, not skipped — it is the promise the design rests on.
items.amber: 1 — 'Next store'. REVISED: the sending motion here is Oatmeal dots, never an amber pulse, and that is now the rule everywhere on the agent surface rather than a local exception.
items.screenshot: An outlined square glyph beside "Submitted. It's on your phone until you have signal." A hairline 'Waiting to send', then three rows — 'Submitted visit', 'Stock count', 'Photo' — each with a state word and a size in monospaced grey, and a small grey line about not guessing the score.

items.name: Reconciliation line — a score that changed after you saw it
items.purpose: When a score the agent already saw is later changed on review, say so in one line instead of letting them find out and stop trusting the app.
items.anatomy: RENAMED AND NARROWED. 44dp min, full gutter width, directly under the hero figure, on the well at radius 10 with a 1px rim, padding 12: a 12dp filled SQUARE glyph (informational, deliberately not a severity), 8dp, then at 13/500 ink-2 'Now scored 71 — it was 84 when you saw it.' with both figures in mono 13; at the right a 44dp ghost 'Why?'. THE PROVISIONAL FIGURE IS DELETED. The critic is right and it resolves the open question rather than escalating it: visit_outcome_screen.dart refuses to show a locally computed score, with a comment explaining exactly why, and this component existed only to give the reconciliation line a referent. It does not need one — a FINAL score the agent saw that later changed on review is a real referent, it already has states elsewhere in this system (SENT BACK on My visits, 'sent back later' on the outcome), and nothing in #374–#400 requires a number to be shown before it is real. The hatched underline and the PROVISIONAL eyebrow go with it; hatch keeps its two honest uses, not measured and can't confirm.
items.states: NO CHANGE — the line does not render. Not 'matches what you saw', which is noise. CHANGED — as above. THE AGENT NEVER OPENED THE OUTCOME — the line does not exist; there is nothing to reconcile, and the new score simply is the score. LARGE CHANGE (>15 points) — a second line names the biggest mover: 'Availability moved most: 84 → 52.' MOVED UP — identical treatment, identical square glyph, no celebration; a surprise upward is as much a trust problem as a surprise downward. WHY SHEET — read-only, listing each dimension that moved with before and after in mono and one plain reason per row from a fixed set ('A section arrived after the score was worked out', 'A photo could not be used', 'A manager reviewed this visit'). There is no dispute button, because the dispute path is a conversation with a manager, not a form.
items.behaviour: The line is never dismissible and never auto-hides — it is part of that visit's record and is still there when the visit is opened from My visits months later. It appears on the next open after the change, never as a push over a screen the agent is working on.
items.modes: Night: well #141D27 with a #5A7088 rim, glyph and text ink-2 #C9C1B1. Day: well #E2DBCC, ink-2 #4A4437. Veld: 56dp, no fill, a 2px #1B2632 border, text 16/600, figures 16/500 mono, 'Why?' a 56dp bordered ghost.
items.accessibility: Announced after the hero: 'Now scored 71. It was 84 when you saw it. Double-tap Why for the detail.' The square glyph is explicitly not announced as a warning and scales to 24dp at 2.0×.
items.amber: None. A reconciliation is information, and information is never amber.
items.screenshot: Directly under a large '71', a slim recessed strip with a small solid square and 'Now scored 71 — it was 84 when you saw it.' in oatmeal, with a small outlined 'Why?' at its right.

items.name: My work — the outbox
items.purpose: Everything the agent has captured and whether the server has it — where 'held on this phone' is the normal state and never an error.
items.anatomy: Header: 'My work' / "Everything you've captured". Sync chip suppressed. BODY (gutter 20): (1) SUMMARY BLOCK — a standalone soft surface with a 1px rim, radius 14, padding 16, always a glyph plus words: ALL SENT / HELD / SENDING / STUCK, each with its own shape and sentence. REVISED: 'Send now' has MOVED from the thumb zone into this block as a 56dp action, because My work is a tab root and tab roots no longer have a thumb zone — and it belongs with the thing it acts on anyway. It is a GHOST by default, because the queue sends itself and pressing it is not the expected next move; it becomes the amber block only when there are stuck items AND connectivity to act on. (2) 32dp. (3) SECTION RULES 'Needs you' / 'Waiting' / 'Sent' — a group with nothing in it prints NO rule. (4) Live outbox rows under each, Sent capped at 20 with a 64dp ghost 'Show older'. (5) A footer at meta: 'Nothing is lost when you close the app. Everything here is on this phone.' BOTTOM: the tab-root floating row — skin cycle, pill, circle.
items.states: EMPTY. ALL SENT. HELD. SENDING. STUCK. SIGNED OUT (a bad-outlined block above the summary: "You're signed out. Sign in and your 12 held captures will send." plus an amber 'Sign in' — and in this one case the amber moves off 'Send now', because signing in IS the expected move). 200+ ITEMS (ListView.builder; Sent capped; compact formatter). LOAD ERROR (the error grammar with a retry; the footer sentence stays, because it is still true). OFFLINE (identical; only the summary wording changes). A ROW RESOLVING WHILE ON SCREEN (it moves group with a 320ms move, never a jump). 2.0× (rows to ~96dp; the summary's figure and words stack; the nav pill becomes a 2×2 grid on its own row).
items.behaviour: Pull-to-refresh triggers a flush. Rows tap into the outbox sheet. The screen is a stream, so it never needs a manual refresh to be correct. The sending dots are one Ticker subscriber.
items.modes: Day: summary #FAF7F2 with a #857C6B rim and sh1, good #14664A, bad #8C1B2C, held in ink-2. Night: summary #1B2632 with a #5A7088 rim, good #6FE0AE, bad #FF7D8C. REVISED: the Night SENDING summary no longer uses an amber pulsing square. The motion-coded amber 'live' mark is retired from the agent surface entirely — the critic's scenario was exact, with three amber objects on one frame and the biggest of them being the navigation label of the tab the agent was already looking at. Sending is Oatmeal dots plus the word, one grammar, everywhere. Veld: white, gutter 24, block gap 40, summary a 2px-bordered rectangle, rows 72dp with 2px rules, STUCK a solid #7A0F22 tile with white ink, nothing moves.

items.name: Session-ended
items.purpose: A signed-out session is a state, not an error — and the agent must be able to see their held work behind it and keep capturing.
items.anatomy: A BOTTOM SHEET over whatever screen the agent was on, deliberately not a route replacement, so the held work is literally visible behind the scrim. Scrim ground@72%. Sheet: radius 14 top, surface fill, 1px edge-structure, grabber. Content (gutter 20): eyebrow 'SIGNED OUT'; 8dp; headline at title.l 20/600 "You've been signed out."; 12dp; 'This happens after a while. Your work is safe.'; 24dp; a 64dp soft row — a filled square glyph, '12 captures held on this phone' with the count in mono, a chevron, tappable through to My work; 24dp; ACTIONS: amber 'Sign in again' 56dp, 8dp, ghost 'Not now' 56dp.
items.states: FIRST APPEARANCE — non-dismissible: the scrim ignores taps, back is consumed, the grabber is hidden so the affordance does not lie. SECOND AND LATER — scrim-dismissible, grabber present. 'NOT NOW' TAKEN — the sheet closes, the agent stays exactly where they were and can keep capturing, because capture is a local write; a persistent 44dp line then appears under every agent header with a square glyph, 'Signed out — work is saving locally', and an inline 44dp ghost 'Sign in'. MID-VISIT — one added line: 'You can carry on with this visit. It will send once you sign in.' NOTHING HELD — the held-work row is absent. SIGN-IN FAILED — the sheet STAYS OPEN with a bad-outlined line above the actions. RE-AUTH SUCCEEDED — a 200ms exit and a 44dp receipt beneath: 'Signed in — sending 12 captures.'
items.behaviour: Triggered by a 401/403 on any call or by locally detected token expiry. It NEVER appears more than once per two minutes, so a burst of 401s from a flushing queue does not stack sheets. It never carries an error icon, a red fill, the word 'Error' or a status code.

Veld: white with a 2px border on all sides, radius 0, scrim a solid #1B2632 at 90%, headline 22/700, body 17/600, actions 64dp at 18/700.
items.accessibility: scopesRoute and namesRoute, focus trapped, route named 'Signed out'. Announced as "You've been signed out. Your work is safe. 12 captures held on this phone." 'Not now' carries 'Stay signed out for now and keep working'. The persistent header line is a liveRegion on first appearance and silent thereafter.
items.amber: 1 — 'Sign in again'.
items.screenshot: A visit hub dimmed behind a panel with rounded top corners: 'SIGNED OUT' small, "You've been signed out." bold, a grey sentence, a row with a solid square reading '12 captures held on this phone' with a chevron, then a wide amber 'Sign in again' over an outlined 'Not now'.

items.name: Decision sheet — resuming an interrupted visit
items.purpose: Carry on or start over, asked with enough evidence that the choice is informed — and weighted, because the two answers are not equal.
items.anatomy: A bottom sheet, not a dialog — a centred dialog with two equal buttons is exactly how a destructive choice gets tapped by accident. Content (gutter 20): eyebrow 'UNFINISHED VISIT'; 8dp; headline at title.l 20/600 naming the outlet; 20dp; THE EVIDENCE, three 56dp rows separated by rules, figures in mono — 'Checked in 07:42 · 41 minutes ago' / '5 of 8 sections captured' / '3 photos · about 1,4 MB held'; 24dp; ACTIONS: amber 'Carry on' 56dp, 8dp, ghost 'Start over' 56dp, then a 44dp text row 'Not now — go to my route.'
items.states: NORMAL. START OVER TAPPED — the content CROSS-FADES over 200ms to a second step in the same sheet, never a second sheet: 'Starting over deletes 5 captured sections and 3 photos from this phone. They have not been sent.' plus a ghost with a 1px bad outline, 'Delete and start over', plus a ghost 'Keep it'. Two taps and a named consequence — no typed confirmation, which is too much friction in a shop. CHECK-IN OLDER THAN 12 HOURS — 'Carry on' demotes to a ghost and an amber 'Check in again' appears, because a geofence fix from yesterday is not evidence of being here now; the captured work is preserved and re-attached to the new check-in, and the re-attachment is recorded as a resumed visit rather than silently producing captures that predate their own check-in. ZERO SECTIONS CAPTURED — the evidence rows collapse and both actions merge into one amber 'Check in again'. MULTIPLE DRAFTS — the headline becomes 'You have 3 unfinished visits' and the body up to 3 tappable 64dp rows, newest first. DRAFT FOR AN OUTLET NO LONGER ON THE ROUTE — a neutral flag chip 'Not on today's plan'. OFFLINE — identical; the draft is local. DISMISSED — the draft is untouched and the sheet returns on the next app open, because an unfinished visit does not go away by being ignored.
items.behaviour: Shown on app open when a draft exists for an unsubmitted outlet — once per open, never mid-capture. 'Carry on' routes to the hub with the receipt 'Carrying on from 07:42'. The delete path removes the local rows and says so: 'Started over. The old captures are gone.'

Day: #FAF7F2 with a #857C6B rim, destructive #8C1B2C, 'Carry on' a solid amber block. Veld: white with a 2px border at radius 0, headline 22/700, evidence rows 64dp with 2px rules at 16/600, actions 64dp, and the destructive ghost becomes a solid #7A0F22 block with white ink, because a crimson outline on white is the first thing sun erases.

The destructive label names the consequence in full, so a reader is never asked to confirm the word 'Delete'. The second step is a liveRegion.

items.name: Skip-reason picker
items.purpose: Let an agent say why a section cannot be captured, so the fourth state is an answer rather than a gap — and so the answer has a consequence the agent can see.
items.anatomy: A bottom sheet. Content (gutter 20): eyebrow "CAN'T CONFIRM"; 8dp; headline at title.l 20/600 'Why not?'; 20dp; three 64dp rows separated by rules, each a radio (a 28dp ring, 48dp at 2.0×, with a 14dp filled disc when chosen) plus a two-line column — the reason at title.m and beneath it at meta 12 what it does downstream: 'The store would not let me' → 'The manager is told the store refused'; 'They do not stock this' → 'These lines are marked not-stocked for this outlet'; 'The equipment is broken' → 'A repair task is raised'. A fourth row 'Something else' reveals a required 3-line trough, max 200 characters, counter past 160. ACTIONS: amber 'Save reason' 56dp, disabled until a choice exists; ghost 'Cancel'.
items.states: NOTHING CHOSEN (primary disabled, its label appending 'choose a reason first'). CHOSEN. SOMETHING ELSE, TEXT EMPTY (still disabled; the trough shows no error until a save is attempted). SAVING. SAVED (the sheet closes; the section takes the hatched state, the reason becomes the hub row's detail line, the section stops blocking submit, AND — NEW — a row for it appears on the submit gate under 'What this raises'). THIRD CAN'T-CONFIRM IN ONE VISIT — a 44dp line in the sheet before saving: 'That will be three sections you could not confirm. Your manager sees that as a store you could not work.' No block, no scold; the agent simply knows what the manager will see. ALL REQUIRED SECTIONS REACHED — the line reads 'That is every required section. The visit will be recorded as a store you could not work, not as a completed visit.' ALREADY SET (pre-selected, the primary reads 'Change reason', plus a ghost 'Remove — I can confirm it after all'). SAVE FAILED (the sheet STAYS OPEN with a bad-outlined line). OFFLINE (unchanged; the reason queues like any capture). FROM CHECK-IN (opened by "I can't get closer": the reasons become 'The store is closed', 'I cannot get to the store', 'The store refused the visit', and saving records a skipped stop). 2.0× (rows to ~96dp).
items.behaviour: Choosing a row selects it and moves focus to the primary, so the flow is two taps. 'Something else' expands in place over 200ms. The sheet is dismissible; dismissing changes nothing.
items.modes: Night: radio border #7C93AC, disc #EEE9DF, 'Save reason' lifted with an amber rim. Day: border #6E6657, disc #1B2632, a solid amber block. Veld: white with a 2px border at radius 0, rows 72dp with 2px rules, reason 18/600, consequence 14/600, radio 32dp with a 3px border, primary a 64dp amber block at 18/700.
items.accessibility: Each row is Semantics(inMutuallyExclusiveGroup:true, selected:) announcing the reason AND its consequence: "The store would not let me. The manager is told the store refused. Radio button, 1 of 4, not selected." The disabled primary keeps its label and states why. The threshold line is a liveRegion.

items.name: My visits
items.purpose: The agent's own record — what they did, what it scored, and honestly what has not been scored yet.
items.anatomy: Header: 'My visits' / 'Last 30 days'. BODY (gutter 20): (1) a 1×2 stat cluster divided by a 1px hairline, collapsing on a LayoutBuilder width threshold, both cells built from the stat-tile component so either can admit no data. (2) 32dp. (3) SECTION RULE 'This week', then visit rows, 64dp, separated by the 3:1 tappable rule: a 28dp tile carrying the band glyph or a HATCHED tile when unscored; outlet name at title.m wrapping to 2; meta 'Thu 18 Sep · 41 min · 3 tasks raised' with figures in mono; right, the score in mono 16/600, or an em dash with 'not scored yet' in the meta line — never a bare dash. (4) Further rules per week. (5) A 64dp ghost 'Show older'. BOTTOM: the 76dp skin-cycle-only zone, because this screen has no primary action and must still reach Veld.
items.states: LOADING (skeleton). EMPTY. OFFLINE (local data plus a 44dp square-glyph line: "Showing what's on this phone. 12 captures haven't sent."). UNSCORED VISIT (hatched tile, 'Waiting to be scored'). SENT BACK (a flag chip, 1px bad outline, half-filled triangle — the one flag that is a severity). SKIPPED / COULD NOT WORK (NEW, matching the new gate state: a hatched tile, 'Could not work this store — store refused', and no score column at all rather than a dash, because it was never scoreable). A WEEK WITH NO VISITS (its rule is simply absent). LOAD ERROR (cached list plus a square-glyph line). 100+ VISITS (ListView.builder, paged). 2.0× (rows to ~104dp; the cluster collapses).
items.behaviour: Tapping a row opens the outcome READ-ONLY: no 'Next store', a ghost 'Back', and the reconciliation line where there was a change. Pull-to-refresh. Rows never reorder while on screen. Nothing is editable — a submitted visit is closed.

Veld: white, gutter 24, block gap 40, the cluster split by a 2px rule, rows 64dp with 2px rules, name 18/600, meta 14/600, the tile 32dp with a 2px border, 'Sent back' a solid #7A0F22 with white ink.

items.name: What I've earned
items.purpose: Points, the reward they lead to, and where each one came from — with the same honesty about numbers as the score screen.
items.anatomy: Header: "What I've earned" / 'September'. BODY (gutter 20): (1) the PROGRESS-TO-REWARD BAR at the top — the reason the screen exists. (2) 32dp. (3) a 1×2 stat cluster split by a hairline: 'POINTS THIS MONTH · 1 840' and 'RANK · 4 of 22' with the rank in mono. (4) 32dp. (5) SECTION RULE 'How you earned it'. (6) the ledger: 64dp rows separated by the 3:1 tappable rule — a 28dp tile with a 2px-stroke glyph per source, the reason at 15/600 wrapping to 2, meta 'Thu 18 Sep · score 78' in mono, and right, '+12' in mono with a solid up triangle; a reversal shows '−5' with a down triangle in bad and the reason spelled out. (7) a 44dp honesty line: 'Points are worked out on the server. They can change if a visit is reviewed.' BOTTOM: the 76dp skin-cycle-only zone plus a ghost 'See the leaderboard' where the scheme has one.
items.states: LOADING (skeleton). NO POINTS YET. NO SCHEME RUNNING (the bar is absent entirely and a body line says so — an empty bar would read as zero progress). NOT RANKED (an em dash with 'not ranked yet — fewer than 5 agents have points'). OFFLINE (the bar goes hatched, figures go to em dashes, 'Points update when your work sends'; the ledger renders from cache with a square-glyph line). REWARD REACHED (the fill goes good with a filled circle at the tick and 'Reward reached — R 250 airtime, paid with your next cycle.' Nothing flashes). LEDGER OVER 50 (cursor-paged behind a ghost 'Show more'). LOAD ERROR (cached ledger plus a square-glyph line). 2.0× (the bar's figure and unit stack, the cluster collapses, rows grow).
items.behaviour: The bar animates once per genuine change, not per visit to the screen. The cluster counts up once from a single controller. Tapping a ledger row opens the visit it came from, read-only. Nothing here is a call to action.

openQuestions:
1. RESOLVED, NOT ESCALATED — THE NAV PILL AND THE AMBER LAW. I withdraw the clause I wrote and the owner never saw. On light grounds the pill is NEVER amber: Day active is solid lifted #2C3B4D with Palladian ink (9.43:1), Veld is a solid #1B2632 block with white (15.33:1), and a Day or Veld screen with nothing armed carries zero amber, which is already the rule on My visits and every empty state. Owner decision 3 survives intact where amber can legally be a fill — Night, where #FFB162 with #0B1017 ink is 10.65:1 and the direction spec's own lint rule permits a filled amber block with abyss-000 foreground. The cost is honest and I will not hide it: in Night the active pill IS a semantic amber on a status, which sits uneasily with 'amber is the move, never the state'. It is bounded by being counted — the pill is object #1 of two on any Night tab root — and by the composed-frame lint. What the owner needs to nod at is one sentence, not a new law: the pill is amber in Night only.

2. STILL OPEN, AND IT IS A NUMBER NOBODY OWNS — THE SECTION COUNT. Verified in the code this session: AuditSection has nine members; outletInfo and score both carry entityType: null; captureCount is `values.where(entityType != null).length` plus one for a client template, which is SEVEN, or eight with a template. The brief says nine. The hub lists nine or ten rows. Every mock here says '5 of 8'. Somebody must decide whether the agent-facing figure counts capturable sections (7/8), hub rows (9/10), or something else, and whether outletInfo — auto-completed by the act of checking in — belongs in a denominator at all. I read the readiness block from captureCount and would not change the code to match a number in a brief.

3. STILL OPEN AND STILL THE HIGHEST-RISK TYPOGRAPHY — MONO FIGURES INSIDE ONEST PROSE. Onest has no width axis, so the direction spec's whole wdth 88–112 mechanism is dead under the owner's typeface decision and I have dropped it; the display voice is weight and size only. The live problem is unchanged: '12 SKUs · 2 out of stock', '41 min in store', 'R 24,99' — four or five mono runs per hub row, each a visibly different colour of text inside an Onest sentence. I set them at the prose size with −1% tracking. The alternative breaks the owner's own rule that every figure in a data role is mono. This needs a printed specimen read outdoors at 40% backlight before it is committed, and no amount of specification substitutes for that.

4. RESOLVED — NO PROVISIONAL SCORE. The critic is right and it dissolves the question rather than escalating it. I have deleted the provisional figure treatment entirely and rescoped the reconciliation line to a final score the agent saw that later changed on review, which already has referents in this system. visit_outcome_screen.dart's documented refusal stands untouched and #374–#400 is still served. Nothing needs a number shown before it is real.

5. STILL OPEN AND STILL A ROADMAP CALL — PHASE 2 CAPTURE. pubspec.yaml has image_picker and no camera package; photo_capture_service.dart hands off to the OS camera. If Phase 2 is not funded, the amber brackets, the 72dp shutter, the 56dp torch and the in-app preview never ship, and the agent's capture is the stock Android camera preceded by a reminder card — materially worse than this document reads. It also forces the torch reminder onto solar elevation plus the LAST capture's luma rather than the current frame's, which is a worse trigger. Phase 1 is specified honestly as its own screen rather than as a degraded Phase 2; decide the roadmap before anyone reviews the Phase 2 item as if it were shipping.

6. STILL OPEN, NOW PARTLY BOUNDED — VELD × 2.0× × AFRIKAANS. The header cap I added (subtitle 2 lines, flags 2 rows plus an expander, a 40% viewport ceiling past which the header scrolls) fixes the worst case the critic found, where a hub header ate 370dp of a 640dp screen and left room for two ladder rows. The scroll-length question survives: an Afrikaans stop row at p90 wrapping to two lines at 18/600 is roughly 96dp, 128dp at 2.0×, so an 11-stop Veld route is over 1 400dp. That may simply be correct — Veld halves density on purpose — but it should be measured on a real route before we call it a feature. If it fails, the fix is a Veld-only collapsed stop row (name and distance, no code), which I have deliberately not designed speculatively.

7. NARROWED TO A BACKEND DECISION — THE OUTBOX PAYLOAD SIZE. SyncQueueItems stores payloadJson and nothing computes a byte size. I have decided the design side: show the DECODED size prefixed 'about', because the whole reason the figure is on the row is an agent deciding whether to send on a 1 GB bundle, and base64 length overstates a photo by ~33% in exactly the direction that matters. What is still open is whether the backend will store a decoded size on enqueue. If it will not, the figure comes off the row rather than being shown wrong.

8. STILL OPEN, AND IT BLOCKS BUILDING THE DECISION SHEET — RESUMED VISITS VERSUS THE FRAUD MODULE. The stale-fix branch preserves captured work and re-attaches it to a new check-in, which is the right agent experience; the alternative destroys real work because a fix is twelve hours old. It produces a visit whose captures predate its check-in, which is precisely the shape stock_outside_outlet and failed_attempts are built to notice. A server-side 'resumed visit' marker is needed before the sheet is built, or we ship a feature that flags every agent who uses it.

9. NEW, AND IT IS NOW THE LARGEST OPEN DEPENDENCY — WILL THE SERVER ACCEPT A NULL COUNT? The single most consequential fix in this revision is that an uncounted SKU must send null rather than zero, so that eight products nobody looked at stop becoming eight out-of-stock findings against a store on one tap of Save. The client already has the state and the scorecard already has the unmeasured grammar. If the server cannot take null this cycle, the fallback ships instead — a blocking two-step where the destructive option names itself, 'Save 4 counts and record 8 as out of stock' — and that is a worse product. This needs an answer before the stock section is built, not after.

10. NEW AND SMALL — WHERE DOES HANDEDNESS LIVE? Moving the ± pair adjacent to the trailing edge fixes the grip-shift, but it is right-hand-default, and a left-handed agent should be able to mirror it once in Me. That is a stored user preference, not a device setting, and nothing in the app stores per-agent UI preferences yet. If we are not prepared to add one, the pair stays trailing for everyone and I would rather know that than design a setting that has nowhere to live.
principles: Darkness is the site, not the style — but the agent defaults to Day, and Veld is one thumb-tap away in the only region a hand holding a crate can reach, which is why the skin cycle is on every screen including the tab roots. Amber is the move, never the state: counted as objects in the composed frame, one on light grounds, two in Night, zero where there is no next move. Severity is mass, shape and words — a filled triangle, a 3px bar, a sentence — never hue alone. Every shape that carries meaning scales with the text. Nothing is perceived by a fill step alone: rows and blocks that a thumb can press carry an edge at 3:1. Held work is normal and never red. The app never reports what nobody looked at. Nothing is centred except the shutter.
